The Theory System catalogues and revalidates theories across domains.\nContexts bind scope and authority. Profiles realize the architecture. It describes how typed operations compose. AAP is the\nprocess compiler/router: it chooses the minimum sufficient architecture subgraph, assurance depth, resources,\nauthorities and fallbacks for the requested operation. The Universal Per-Step Control Loop governs every meaningful\ntransition inside the compiled process.\n\nCanonical execution spine:\n\n  Human / Event / Trigger\n    → typed intent and context\n    → Process Algebra expression\n    → AAP classification and capability/dependency closure\n    → ProcessPlan\n    → TransitionStep*\n    → authorized effect / derivation / communication\n    → observation and expected-vs-actual comparison\n    → receipt / knowledge update / recovery / learning\n    → next state.\n\nUniversal TransitionStep loop:\n\n  Observe\n    → Understand / Type\n    → Compare\n    → Reason\n    → candidate generation\n    → Select\n    → Guard selected transition\n    → Execute / Derive / Communicate\n    → Observe resulting state\n    → Compare expected vs actual\n    → Update / Correct / Retry / Replan / Research / Escalate / Learn / Terminate.\n\nA cheap pre-selection constraint filter may remove obviously inadmissible candidates before Select. The canonical\neffect gate still evaluates the selected candidate before any effect. This resolves the conceptual shorthand\n\"Guard → Select\" without permitting an unguarded selected action.\n\nMeaningful transition boundary:\nThe universal loop applies at semantic process boundaries, not recursively to every CPU instruction or neural\nactivation. A transition is meaningful when it creates or materially changes persistent/canonical state, external\neffects, a decision/branch, authority, epistemic status, resource commitment, consequential communication, or another\ndeclared process boundary. Lower implementation operations inherit the enclosing verified contract unless separately\nelevated by AAP, risk or policy.\n\nThree activation classes:\n  CLASS 1 — UNIVERSAL SEMANTIC / CONTROL KERNEL\n    GSL/semantic typing; Context; Time; Compare; Reason; Dependency; Verity/Proof; Safety;\n    Constitution/Rights; AAP; Events/Provenance; Authority for externally meaningful effects.\n\n  CLASS 2 — CONTEXT-TRIGGERED CROSS-CUTTING CAPABILITIES\n    Privacy; Policy; Law; Compliance; Access; Governance; Continuity; Emergency;\n    Economy/Resource Allocation; Explanation; and future predicate-triggered cross-cutting services.\n\n  CLASS 3 — DOMAIN / EXECUTION CAPABILITIES\n    Mathematics; Research; Search; Software; Hardware; Network; Fabric; Energy; Mobility; Space;\n    Health/Medicine; Industry; Education; Quantum; and any other applicable domain/runtime capability.\n\nCentral rule:\nGarden is a typed capability graph whose requested operations are compiled by AAP under Process Algebra into the\nsmallest sufficient process graph. Every meaningful process transition then executes as a tiered, compared, reasoned,\nguarded, observed and recorded state transition.\n\nWhen a semantic transition benefits from a numerical/vector/matrix/tensor/operator representation, AAP may activate\nAlgebra.Bridge to produce the applicable operator/representation/compute path. Bridge is conditional rather than a\nmandatory heavyweight step; it cannot bypass the parent Process, assurance, authority or epistemic contracts.\n\nARTIFACT-CATALOGUE & GENERATION PRINCIPLE\nThe human design defines semantic contracts and stable artifact identities.         "content": "SemanticAnchor: [T-GSL]\n\n2.1 CANONICAL ONTOLOGY\n\nSix Pillars\n Existence · Change · Agency · Law · Value · Frame\n\nTen Core Objects\n TIME = instant/interval, ordering, validity and actual/simulation branch.\n SPACE = coordinates/region/reference system/parent space.\n THING = universal semantic root with stable identity/name/type/version.\n EVENT = occurrence in the modeled world/state-transition history. An ObservationRecord or AttestedObservation is an\n ARTIFACT that may reference an EVENT; recording or observing an occurrence does not become the occurrence itself.\n ACTION = intentional state-changing operation with actor/preconditions/status.\n AGENCY = actor/authority/capability/delegation/accountability semantics.\n RULE = tiered condition → conclusion/constraint.\n VALUE = semantic Fact | Preference | Norm. Representation is orthogonal; VALUE is not universally a Decimal.\n CONTEXT = frame containing scope, risk class, active rules, environment and interpretation conditions.\n CLAIM = assertion with subject/predicate/object, evidence references, disposition, confidence?,\n provenance, validity_scope, and version. Claim is the primary unit of epistemic state.\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-CFD2F543E6 — Claim..\nTHING subtype registry\n ENTITY = Person | Organization | Community | Locality | Device | Infrastructure | Garden |\n extensible typed descendants.\n ARTIFACT = Document | Dataset | Model | Software | Media | Contract | Credential | Proof | WorkPackage |\n TheoryArtifact | LanguageArtifact | Observation | extensible typed descendants.\n\nInvariant references: ONT-001..004.\nHumanCore.DelegatedAgent means the AI agent acting for the user. GSL AGENCY is the semantic/ontological object; Agent ≠\nAgency.\n\n2.2 CURRENT 24 CORE RELATIONS\n\nFoundational (10)\n identifies, causes, governs, values, frames, acts, obeys, assesses, contextualizes, controls\n\nPractical / lineage (14)\n partOf, dependsOn, owns, delegates, references, derivedFrom, equivalentTo, contradicts,\n supports, blocks, hasHypothesis, supersedes, conflictsWith, originatesFrom\n\nKey algebraic rules\n equivalentTo symmetric + transitive; cycles permitted.\n partOf transitive + antisymmetric; cycles forbidden.\n dependsOn is kind-qualified: build/order dependencies are transitive over the admitted build DAG and cycles are forbidden; runtime/semantic dependencies may contain an explicitly declared strongly-connected feedback/fixed-point group only under registered semantics, admissible initialization, and required termination/service-liveness evidence. Antisymmetry applies to the acyclic/condensed dependency order, not raw nodes inside an admitted feedback SCC.\n derivedFrom directed lineage; cycles forbidden.\n controls authority/control edge; cycles forbidden.\n supersedes directional/version aware; cycles forbidden; predecessor remains immutable.\n originatesFrom directed provenance; cycles forbidden.\n contradicts symmetric semantic opposition; cycles permitted.\n conflictsWith symmetric declared conflict; cycles permitted, explicit resolution required.\n causes feedback cycles permitted.\n references cycles permitted.\n delegates capability(delegate) ⊆ capability(principal).\n supports does not by itself promote epistemic status.\n\nCanonical composition candidates include:\n delegates ∘ acts → acts\n owns ∘ controls → derivedControl\n supports ∘ supports → candidate indirect support; it becomes supports only through an explicit valid warrant.\n causes ∘ causes → causalPath; it becomes a causal Claim only under a valid causal model, compatible\n context, and declared assumptions.\n hasHypothesis ∘ assesses → evaluatedHypothesis\nAll undeclared normative compositions raise CompositionError or require an explicit domain rule. Non-core\nlineage/domain vocabulary does not silently become one of the 24 Core Relations.\n\nInvariant references: REL-ALG-001..002.\n2.3 TWELVE GSL CORE SEMANTIC PRIMITIVES + TWO GARDEN EXECUTION-CONTROL PRIMITIVES\n\nSTATUS: NORMATIVE — CROSS-CUTTING SEMANTIC / EXECUTION-CONTROL REGISTRY\n\nGSL v45.1 defines twelve core semantic primitive families. Garden uses COMPARE and REASON as universal\nexecution-control primitives expressed using existing GSL semantics. The Garden-level total is therefore fourteen,\nwithout changing the ten Core Objects, 24 Core Relations, §12.4 grammar or GSL v45.1 release identity. These\nprimitives govern how typed payloads are observed, transformed, authorized, compared, reasoned about, stored and\nexecuted; they create no competing top-level object.\n\n1. STATE\n S(t) + Event + Action → S(t+1).\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-3583B93887 — DeterministicResolutionContext..\n Determinism is conditional on the declared context and inputs. Missing nondeterministic physical or\n external inputs are modeled explicitly; they are not silently replaced by a seed.\n\n2. OBSERVATION\n Observation ≠ Evidence ≠ Claim ≠ Knowledge.\n\n ObservationSource = SensorAttested(SensorAttestationRef) | Human | Document | System | Model.\n A sensor attestation binds device identity, calibration, time, configuration, integrity, and\n provenance.\n\n3. AUTHORITY\n Entity → Identity → Credential → Role → Capability → Authority → Action.\n\n Capability does not self-create authority. Delegation is scoped, expiring, revocable, auditable,\n and no broader than the principal’s legitimate authority.\n\n4. RESOURCE\n Request → Reserve → Allocate → Consume → Release → Reconcile.\n\n Forecast Resource ≠ Receivable Resource ≠ Liquid Resource ≠ Allocated Resource ≠\n Committed Resource ≠ Spent Resource ≠ Recovered Resource.\n\n5. ADDRESS\n garden://{namespace}/{type}/{instance}/{version} + content hash.\n\n Human-readable address, semantic version, validity scope, and immutable content identity are\n separately represented.\n\n6. PROVENANCE\n Source + DirectedLineageGraph + cryptographic roots/anchors.\n\n Provenance is a typed graph, not a single source string. It supports backward explanation,\n forward impact analysis, privacy-aware disclosure, and cryptographic/institutional attestation.\n\n7. CAUSALITY\n C0 Correlation | C1 Temporal | C2 Mechanistic | C3 Intervention | C4 Counterfactual.\n\n No higher level is inferred from a lower one without the declared causal model, assumptions,\n evidence, identification conditions, and uncertainty.\n\n8. DEPENDENCY\n Build DAG | Runtime dependency | Semantic dependency.\n\n Cycles require an explicit permitted semantics, fixed-point/feedback interpretation where\n applicable, and termination/liveness proof. Undeclared cycles are rejected.\n\n9. CONFLICT\n Argument | Authority | Governance | CRDT | HardcodedFallback.\n\n Conflict is typed and auditable. SAME, REFINEMENT, COMPATIBLE, CONTEXT_DIFFERENT, APPROXIMATION,\n TRUE_CONTRADICTION, and UNRESOLVED are distinct results. UNRESOLVED is valid.\n\n10. UNCERTAINTY\n Epistemic (potentially reducible) versus aleatoric (model-irreducible within the declared model).\n\n Neither uncertainty type weakens K0P or Constitution. Representation follows the Mathematical\n Representation Policy; interval, distribution, vector, tensor, symbolic, and domain-specific\n forms are not silently collapsed to one confidence number.\n\n11. DECISION\n Recommendation | Authorization | Commitment | Execution.\n\n The stages are not interchangeable. Recommendation ≠ Authorization. Authorization without a\n valid commitment/execution path is not execution. Execution does not prove the recommendation\n was epistemically correct.\n\n12. VALIDITY\n Version = semantic revision identity. Validity = time/context/scope.\n\n Version and validity are orthogonal. The same version may have different validity scopes; a new\n version does not automatically invalidate all predecessor uses.\n\n13. COMPARE — GARDEN EXECUTION-CONTROL PRIMITIVE\n COMPARE(A, B, dimensions, context) → ComparisonResult.\n\n Compare performs typed difference, similarity, dominance, conflict, materiality and uncertainty analysis. It is used\n before consequential selection where alternatives/targets exist and after effectful transitions to compare expected\n and observed state. Comparison never creates truth, evidence, authority or permission merely by ranking candidates.\n\n Comparison may evaluate actual vs expected/desired state; candidate vs candidate; claim vs evidence; prediction vs\n observation; action vs constraints; cost vs benefit; risk vs permissible risk; current vs alternative design; new vs\n existing knowledge; and result vs success condition.\n\n Schema reference: SCHEMA-2D736A85E2 — ComparisonResult.\n\n14. REASON — GARDEN EXECUTION-CONTROL PRIMITIVE\n REASON(problem, context, candidates, tier) → ReasoningTrace | InferenceResult | UNKNOWN.\n\n Reason determines what follows, what alternatives exist, what should be selected within legitimate constraints, and\n what further evidence or verification is required. It is logically present at every meaningful transition, while AAP\n selects R0..R4 depth. Reasoning remains distinct from Proof, Evidence, Authorization and Execution.\n\nRELATION TO THE 10 CORE OBJECTS\nThe 10 Core Objects (TIME, SPACE, THING, EVENT, ACTION, AGENCY, RULE, VALUE, CONTEXT, CLAIM) are the atomic payload\nfamilies. The twelve GSL v45.1 primitives plus the two Garden execution-control primitives govern how those payloads are\ncreated, observed, transformed, stored, authorized, allocated, compared and reasoned about. Every Garden operation uses\none or more primitive families through UPA/GTF profiles.\n\nInvariant references: PRIM-001..003.\n2.4 PRIMARY STRUCTURAL ARTIFACT TYPES\nThe current GSL v45.1 structural layer comprises Evidence, ProofTrace, Resolution, and Explanation.\nCLAIM is a Core Object in §2.1. The following schemas are the current authoritative structural registry:\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-EF8A522F4B — Evidence.; SCHEMA-E76B9B1661 — ProofTrace.; SCHEMA-D47AED8D50 — Resolution.;\n                   SCHEMA-EF09AC3E7E — Explanation..\nInvariant references: STR-001..003.\n2.5 MASTER / LANGUAGE INVARIANTS\nCanonical definitions: Annexure A.\nInvariant references: G-001..010, LANG-001..009, GSL-STAT-001..011.\nNo separate “eight GSL axioms” set is active in the current design.\n\n2.6 K-INT GLOBAL EPISTEMIC INVARIANTS\nCanonical definitions: Annexure A.\nInvariant references: K-INT-001..018.\n2.7 EFFECT / TYPE / EPISTEMIC SYSTEM\nClosed effect dimensions:\n Computational, Safety, Auth/Authority, Privacy, Temporal, Resource, Uncertainty, Continuity, Optimization.\nConflicting effects produce INFEASIBLE rather than arbitrary compromise. Effect ordering is compile-time enforced.\n\nEpistemic basis:\n Formal | Empirical | Statistical | Testimonial | Inference | Hypothesis.\nDisposition:\n PROVEN | VERIFIED | SUPPORTED | UNVERIFIED | RETRACTED | CONTRADICTED | UNKNOWN.\nUNKNOWN subtypes:\n CONFLICT_UNKNOWN | EVIDENCE_UNKNOWN | UNDECIDABLE | RESOURCE_UNKNOWN | STALE_UNKNOWN |\n MODEL_INVALID_UNKNOWN | SCOPE_UNDEFINED_UNKNOWN.\nUNKNOWN ≠ NOT_APPLICABLE ≠ FALSE ≠ SAFE.\n\nEvidence merge considers disposition, strength, independence, method, scope, freshness and provenance. Correlated\nagreement is not independent confirmation. SCC/circular-support analysis prevents a mutually supporting cycle with no\nindependent grounding from self-promoting.\n\n2.7A FORMAL TYPE, EFFECT, SCOPE, AUTHORITY AND REFERENCE SYSTEM\n\nJudgment form:\n  Γ ; Δ ; A ; C ⊢ e : T ! ε\n\nwhere Γ is the value/type environment, Δ the dependency/schema environment, A the authority/capability environment,\nC the context/DesignEpoch binding, T the result type and ε the closed effect vector.\n\nCore rules:\n- Every canonical field has a declared type or a TypeResolutionEntry; unresolved names are compile errors.\n- Ref<T> is a typed content-addressable reference carrying target kind, immutable identity/hash, version, validity,\n  DesignEpoch and provenance. EvidenceRef, ProofRef, TheoryRef, ActionRef and similar names are aliases of Ref<T>.\n- Subtyping is explicit nominal/refinement subtyping. Scope widening, authority widening and epistemic promotion are not\n  ordinary subtyping operations.\n- Effect dimensions are Computational, Safety, Authority, Privacy, Temporal, Resource, Uncertainty, Continuity and\n  Optimization. Composition joins effects and preserves the most restrictive applicable hard requirement.\n- Authority is capability- and scope-based. Capability possession does not prove legitimacy; execution still requires\n  Constitution/Rights, K0P, authenticity, authorization, consent and policy gates where applicable.\n- Bool is used only for total deterministic predicates with complete true/false semantics. Epistemic, proof, safety,\n  policy, compliance, migration and distributed outcomes use declared multi-status algebras.\n- Money, rates, physical quantities, probability, risk, intervals/distributions and calibrated measurements use semantic\n  types. Raw machine floating point is an implementation representation under Represented<T>, never a universal type.\n- Generated aliases, enums and owner-qualified domain types resolve through the Artifact Catalogue, machine-projection\n  generation rules and the generated TypeResolutionRegistry.\n- Type/effect preservation, progress or explicit terminal status, reference integrity, authority non-amplification and\n  dependency closure are proof obligations for the admitted compiler profile.\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-2AFAC82F5D — GSLTypeSystemProfile.; SCHEMA-E1FBF0D84D — TypeResolutionEntry.;\n                   SCHEMA-5FE2DD0C69 — TypeResolutionRegistry.\n\n2.8 CORE ALGEBRAS\nSchema references: SCHEMA-EE8B487BB1 — Transition.; SCHEMA-4A4A42095B — Contract..\nOutcome = Success | Rejected | Infeasible | Timeout | Unknown | Conflict | Failure | Quarantined | Escalated\nSchema references: SCHEMA-F89319FBC1 — Epistemic.; SCHEMA-D28FD57947 — Temporal..\nFormal semantics are represented through three mutually checked views:\n Op : operational semantics (state, expression) → (state', value)\n Den : denotational mapping Type → mathematical object (set/probability/Hilbert/etc.)\n Ax : axiomatic/Hoare-style discrete, probabilistic and continuous contracts.\nTarget D1: operational, denotational and axiomatic semantics agree on the declared fragment; proof discharge remains\npending where not established.\n\n2.9 MATHEMATICAL REPRESENTATION POLICY — CURRENT NORMALIZED FORM\nCore rule: representation ≠ semantic meaning.\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-C222A09D1A — Represented<T>..\nLogOdds = semantic probability representation only.\nLogEvidence = evidence-strength representation; it does not become probability unless a valid model maps it.\nLogRisk = domain risk representation with declared scale/model.\n\nInvariant references: GSL-MATH-001..005.\nRECURSIVE TYPING PRECEDENCE RULE\nCanonical typed semantics override shorthand in detailed prose/profile examples. A raw Float, raw Bool, untyped vector,\nor generic Bytes occurrence in a human-readable detailed schema is not permission to use that representation as the\nmachine semantic type. The machine projection MUST resolve it to the applicable MoneyAmount, ExactDecimal, Rational,\nQuantity<Unit,Frame>, Probability, Rate<Unit>, RiskBound, Interval/Distribution/Tensor/Symbolic representation,\nmulti-status result algebra, typed payload, or other declared domain type before certification. Epistemic, proof,\nsafety, authority, policy and compliance states MUST NOT collapse to Bool where UNKNOWN/INCONCLUSIVE/BLOCKED/STALE or\nother declared outcomes are semantically possible. Any unresolved shorthand is a machine-package conformance failure,\nnot a competing definition of GSL.\n\n2.10 GSL COMPILATION / GRAMMAR\nHuman / External Source\n → GSL semantic parsing\n → AST\n → Type / Effect / Dependency analysis\n → CIR\n → Backend / code generation\n → Binary / runtime representation\n → Proof / Safety / Policy gates\n → Execution\n\nCompiler triad: independently implemented Haskell / Rust / OCaml frontends/backends MUST agree on CIR for the declared\nconsensus profile; divergence → HALT/INVESTIGATE.\n\nNormative grammar authority:\n §12.4 contains the sole current compiler-facing GSL grammar and lexical/precedence contract for this master.\n This section defines the compilation pipeline only. No second local program production is normative.\n Obsolete or external syntax requires explicit offline migration before current compilation/execution.\n\n2.11 CUBE × RING — EXPANDED CURRENT MODEL\n\nGardenState(t) ∈ Cube × Ring.\n\nThe construction is a semantic/state representation and not an additional architecture object, physical claim, or claim\nthat all\nreality is literally a cube or algebraic ring.\n\nCube — simultaneous structured dimensions\n C1 Existence/Thing : entities, artifacts, identity, composition, state.\n C2 Space/Location : coordinate frame, region, topology, containment, adjacency.\n C3 Agency/Authority : actors, roles, capability, delegation, accountability.\n C4 Rule/Constraint : Constitution, law, policy, contract, invariant, proof obligation.\n C5 Value/Epistemic : fact/preference/norm, objective, evidence, uncertainty, status.\n C6 Context/Scope : domain, locale, environment, risk, branch, DesignEpoch, validity.\n\nRing — ordered continuity and change\n R1 Time : instants, intervals, clocks, logical/causal order, expiry.\n R3 Action : authorized operation and declared effects.\n R4 Transition : pre-state, delta, post-state, obligations, rollback/compensation.\n R5 Recurrence : schedules, periodic review, bounded loops, fixed points.\n R6 Causal progression : mechanisms, interventions, counterfactual branches, descendant effects.\n\nCore operators\n project(Cube, dimensions, scope) → scoped state view\n join(view_a, view_b, conflict_policy) → merged view | CONFLICT | UNRESOLVED\n advance(state, transition, DRC) → next state + receipts\n replay(genesis, commits, environment) → reconstructed state | mismatch\n branch(state, delta) → immutable alternative history\n compare(trajectories, objectives) → dominance | incomparability | unresolved\n fold(events, transition_fn) → bounded accumulated state\n trace(effect, lineage_graph) → causes, dependencies, authority, provenance\n\nTemporal/causal relationship\n S[n+1] = T[n](S[n]) is the discrete ledger view.\n For continuous domains, a declared flow Φ over an interval may update state, but its sampled events,\n assumptions, solver/calibration configuration, and approximation error are bound into the Ring.\nTemporal precedence is not causality; causal promotion follows the C0–C4 ladder.\n\nPROJECTION CORRESPONDENCE CONTRACT\nCube × Ring is a typed view over the authoritative Core Object graph, not a second ontology and not automatically a\nglobal isomorphism. A declared fragment may claim lossless correspondence only when a machine-verifiable proof records:\n source graph and registry roots;\n fragment/scope and DesignEpoch;\n Core Object and relation coverage;\n forward and reverse mappings;\n round-trip preservation laws;\n alias/duplication and omission checks;\n information-loss/approximation bounds;\n unresolved or intentionally non-representable content.\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-723F655FA6 — ProjectionCorrespondenceProof.\nFailure of correspondence blocks representation substitution for the affected scope; the authoritative typed graph\nremains controlling. A lossy projection may still be used when its loss is explicit and admissible for the requested\npurpose.\nInvariant references: CXR-001..012.\n2.12 Φ BRIDGE — PERCEPTION → GSL\nNormalized operational profile:\nRaw sensory input\n → AttestedObservation(sensor/device/human identity, calibration, time, environment, integrity, provenance)\n → immutable raw or declared loss-bounded observation retention\n → deadline-class routing\n FAST_SAFETY: bounded local features feed K0P without waiting for rich multimodal fusion\n EPISTEMIC: dependency-aware multimodal fusion under backpressure/resource/deadline budgets\n → feature and hypothesis extraction\n → candidate subject/predicate/object bindings\n → alternative hypotheses + unmodeled remainder\n → localization/synchronization where spatial\n → uncertainty propagation + calibration check\n → provenance/attestation binding\n → ClaimCandidate\n → theory/model applicability routing\n → VALIDATE | UNKNOWN | REJECT/QUARANTINE\n → Knowledge ingress only under K-INT rules.\n\nPhi(Sensory_Input) → ClaimCandidate {\n subject, predicate, object,\n confidence ∈ [0,1]?,\n alternatives: [{hypothesis, confidence}],\n unmodeled_mass,\n calibration_refs, timestamps, localization?, uncertainty,\n provenance\n}\nΣ alternative confidence ≤ 1; remainder is explicit unmodeled alternative space. collective agreement cannot manufacture\n                 truth or rights.\n\n  EPIGENETICS\n    Maps to    : Engine.Evolve, Context, Engine.Reason.\n    Requires   : Versioned context-dependent expression/configuration and inheritance without silent semantic change.\n\n  NEURAL PLASTICITY\n    Maps to    : Capability.Knowledge, Engine.Reason, Engine.Research.\n    Requires   : Continuous revalidation, calibrated learning, dependency-aware adaptation and reversible/reviewable\n                 reconfiguration.\n\n  AUTOPOIESIS\n    Maps to    : Engine.Evolve, Capability.Resilience.Continuity, System Integrity.\n    Requires   : Bounded self-maintenance, repair and recursive regulation while trust roots remain externally\n                 protected.\n\nInvariant references: BIO-001..004.\nThese principles are not optional as review questions. It is a metaphor/formal-design heuristic, not a\nclaim that Garden literally has DNA or that every pair is symmetric.\n\nDOUBLE-HELIX PAIR CARDS\n\n  USER-FACING SOVEREIGN LAYER  ↔  GARDEN SYSTEM\n    Relation : They interact and co-evolve while the person remains a rights-holder, not a system component.\n\n  KNOWLEDGE  ↔  REASON\n    Relation : Knowledge stores and versions epistemic state; Reason transforms/tests it without manufacturing Evidence.\n\n  EVOLVE  ↔  PROOF\n    Relation : Evolution proposes/repairs; Proof verifies declared formal obligations; neither self-certifies.\n\n  CONSTITUTION  ↔  LAW\n    Relation : Constitutional rights constrain legal interpretation and evolution.\n\n  SAFETY  ↔  EMERGENCY\n    Relation : Safety enforces hard boundaries; Emergency uses separately authorized bounded paths and never bypasses\n               Constitution/K0P.\n\n  TIME SERVICE  ↔  EVENT SERVICE\n    Relation : Time orders and scopes; Events record occurrences with clock/provenance bindings.\n\n  INTENT  ↔  POLICY\n    Relation : Intent expresses desired outcomes; Policy constrains legitimate action without becoming truth.\n\nFormalization candidates include dual objects/pairs, adjunctions where mappings genuinely satisfy the required laws,\nproduct structures, and the Cube × Ring recurrence model. Dual numbers may represent local sensitivity in applicable\nmathematical profiles. These are candidate formalisms, not automatically the formal underpinning of every pair; each use\nrequires an explicit mapping and proof/validation.\n\nInvariant references: DHX-001..004.\nThe Double Helix pattern explains why Garden components are interwoven, complementary and self-correcting while\npreserving typed boundaries and independent verification.\n\nSECTION III-B — PROCESS, TRANSITION AND STATE ARCHITECTURE — DETAILED SPECIFICATION\n",

Revalidation is triggered by time, new\nevidence, changed dependencies, changed environment/model, contradiction, high-impact use or explicit audit.\n\nRevalidationPriority(k,t) is domain-policy controlled and must increase with relevant staleness/exposure rather than\nrewarding stale unreviewed knowledge with less scrutiny. A normalized monotone age factor used by this consolidation is:\n AgeFactor_d(a) = 1 + age_weight[d] · ln(1 + a / τ_age[d])\nfor a≥0, age_weight[d]≥0, τ_age[d]>0. The formula records the current direction: older un-revalidated knowledge rises,\nnot falls, in review pressure. Domain criticality, change rate, uncertainty and dependency impact may dominate age.\n\nA priority implementation may combine normalized factors such as:\n Priority ∝ Uncertainty × Importance × DependencyImpact × ChangeExposure × AgeFactor × Criticality\nsubject to bounded, transparent normalization; zeroing one factor must not accidentally suppress a mandatory critical\nreview.\n\n4.2 OUTCOMES\nCONFIRMED | STRENGTHENED | WEAKENED | REFINED | SUPERSEDED | CONTRADICTED | STALE | UNKNOWN | INCONCLUSIVE.\nRevalidation changes interpretation/status while preserving the original historical artifact.\n\n4.3 EPI-007…EPI-012 / KNW-016…018\nCanonical definitions: Annexure A.\nInvariant references: EPI-007..012, KNW-016..018.\n4.4 DAILY EPISTEMIC SWEEP + SATURATION MODEL\nCheap Sweep: scan metadata/dependency/status/freshness across the declared knowledge universe. Budgets: compute,\nmemory, storage, bandwidth, time and money are explicit; exhaustion yields DEFERRED/RESOURCE_UNKNOWN, not “validated”.\nScheduling uses protected critical lanes, per-domain quotas, aging/round-robin fairness, deduplication and retry\nbackoff. A repeatedly deferred high-cost item retains importance but cannot occupy every next slot; its next eligibility\ntime and required resource class are explicit. The request declares a candidate scope, but cannot make itself complete by selecting a convenient\nsubset.\n\nEngine.Dependency/Compliance computes AuditScopeClosure from artifact effects, interfaces, dependencies, active\nprofiles, schemas, theories, contexts, rights, invariants and authority bindings. Depth exhaustion, oscillation, unresolved fatal/critical\n findings, invalid trust state or resource exhaustion automatically abandons/reverts the candidate\n branch to the last accepted state, preserves all evidence, releases the deployment pipeline and\n escalates for independent repair; it is never declared pass.\n - A patch may reduce scope or choose DO_NOTHING/REJECT when compliant repair is unavailable.\n\nAdversarial review rule\n “Survives all attacks” means all applicable attacks in the declared, versioned threat model and\n AdversarialReviewPlan were executed within the stated coverage/resource boundary and left no\n unresolved fatal/critical finding. It does not mean survival against every logically possible or\n future unknown attack. INCONCLUSIVE/RESOURCE_UNKNOWN cannot become SURVIVED by wording or vote.\n\nStatus machine\n REQUESTED → BOUND → AUDITING → FINDINGS\n → PATCHING → REAUDIT ↺ (depth ≤ 3)\n → ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW → FORMAL_CONFORMANCE → CERTIFIED → PREPARED → COMMITTED → MONITORED.\n\nTerminal/exception states\n REJECTED | HALTED | ESCALATED | INCONCLUSIVE | RESOURCE_UNKNOWN | QUARANTINED.\nAccepted exceptions require explicit authority, bounded scope/expiry, do not cover hard Constitution/K0P violations, and\nremain visible in the certificate.\n\nSelf-audit integrity\n The Self-Audit mechanism, registry resolver, patch controller and adversarial orchestrator cannot\n certify changes to themselves. Such changes require a frozen prior verifier, independent\n implementation, immutable test corpus, DesignEpoch transition and external certification authority.\n\nInvariant references: SAP-001..010.\nIntegration\n Primary: Engine.Evolve, Engine.Proof, Engine.Compile, Capability.Platform.Development, Engine.Compliance,\n Engine.Reason, Engine.Dependency, Capability.Trust.Security, Capability.Knowledge, Capability.State.EventService,\n Engine.Transition, Capability.Compute.Runtime.\n Hard gates: Capability.Trust.Safety, HumanCore.Constitution, HumanCore.Privacy, Engine.Policy,\n Capability.Authority.Governance, K0P.\n Proof obligations: P5, P6, P7, P8, P9, P14, P15, P16, P17, P18, P19, P20, P21, P22, P23, P24.\n\nLATE EVOLUTION BINDING\nBranch/Merge Evolution, Historical Counterfactual Optimization, verification/resource efficiency, multi-agent\nchallenge/repair, and convergence experiments are defined once in [T-EVOLVE]. Formal proof ≠ empirical validation.\n\n50.1 UNIFIED REASONING SYSTEM\n\nEngine.Reason\n│\n├── Problem Formalization\n│ └── ProblemSignature\n│\n├── Reasoning Mode Registry\n│ ├── Four Foundational Inference Families\n│ └── Specialized / Composed Modes\n│\n├── Theory Registry\n│ └── TheorySignature + TheoryDependencyGraph\n│\n├── Assumption Registry\n├── Evidence Graph\n├── Inference / Proof Graph\n├── Mode Selection\n├── Mode Composition\n├── Falsification / Challenge\n├── Uncertainty Propagation\n├── Resource / Termination Control\n├── Proof Handoff\n├── Explanation Handoff\n└── Meta-Reasoning\n\n50.2 FOUR FOUNDATIONAL INFERENCE FAMILIES\n\n1. ABDUCTION\n Inference to a candidate/best explanation.\n\n2. ARGUMENTATION\n Dialectical reasoning using attack/defense structures, including Dung\n Grounded / Preferred / Stable semantics.\n\n3. DEDUCTION\n Necessary consequence under declared premises, axioms and formal calculus.\n\n4. EMPIRICAL INDUCTION\n Generalization from observations/evidence with quantified uncertainty.\n\nCritical distinction:\n EMPIRICAL INDUCTION ≠ MATHEMATICAL INDUCTION.\nMathematical induction is a deductive FORMAL_PROOF strategy, not empirical generalization.\n\n50.3 FIRST-CLASS REASONING MODE REGISTRY\n\nTop-level ReasoningMode values:\n DEDUCTIVE\n INDUCTIVE_EMPIRICAL\n ABDUCTIVE\n ARGUMENTATIVE\n ANALOGICAL\n DEFAULT_NONMONOTONIC\n PROBABILISTIC\n CAUSAL\n COUNTERFACTUAL\n TEMPORAL\n SPATIAL\n CONSTRAINT\n DECISION\n ETHICAL_NORMATIVE\n GAME_THEORETIC\n OPTIMIZATION\n PLANNING\n EXPLANATORY\n ADVERSARIAL\n THEORY_REASONING\n FORMAL_PROOF\n MODELING\n PREDICTIVE\n META\n\nPROBABILISTIC subprofiles include:\n BAYESIAN | LIKELIHOOD | GRAPHICAL_MODEL | STATISTICAL\n\nThe current registry therefore contains 24 top-level modes. Counts are descriptive rather than constitutional: a future\nmode refinement does not change the typed architecture registry.\n\n50.4 CORE STATE\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-DE7116FF74 — ReasonState..\nCache validity MUST bind at least:\n DesignEpoch\n KnowledgeSnapshot\n EnvironmentCommitment\n DependencyClosure\n AssumptionSet\n FormalSystemVersion\nA cache hit whose binding is stale is invalid.\n\n50.5 CORE ARTIFACTS\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-3625DC2AA3 — ProblemSignature.; SCHEMA-80D86FE2A7 — TheoryStatus.; SCHEMA-0798799B08 —\n                   ReasoningTrace.; SCHEMA-0C0C4C33EF — EvidenceSet.; SCHEMA-06B084334D — UnknownSubtype..\n50.6 EXISTING THEORY-ORCHESTRATION FUNCTIONS — RETAINED\n\nFormalize(query: Query) → ProblemSignature\n Precondition: query GSL-typed.\n Postcondition: well-formed ProblemSignature.\n\nRetrieve(signature: ProblemSignature) → Set<Theory>\n Uses Engine.Search L0/L1/L2 retrieval/applicability path.\n Structural match is primary; keyword similarity alone is insufficient.\n\nFalsify(theory: Theory, budget: ResourceLimits) → FalsificationResult\n Searches for counterexamples/assumption failures.\n Survival ≠ proof.\n\nCompose(theories: Set<Theory>) → Theory\n Requires compatibility of variables, assumptions, units, scope, uncertainty,\n boundary conditions and validity domains.\n\nManageEvidence(evidence: Evidence) → EvidenceSet\n Evidence remains provenance-bound; LLMs cannot manufacture Evidence.\n\n50.7 DEDUCTION ENGINE\n\nDeduce(\n premises: Set<GSL_Expr>,\n query: GSL_Expr,\n calculus: FormalSystem,\n budget: InferenceBudget\n) → DeductionResult\n\nPreconditions:\n - premises and query are well-formed GSL expressions;\n - the formal system/calculus is declared;\n - assumptions and applicability scope are explicit.\n\nSupported deductive strategies include:\n propositional reasoning; first-order reasoning; predicate reasoning;\n syllogistic reasoning; forward chaining; backward chaining;\n modus ponens; modus tollens; contrapositive; contradiction;\n proof by cases; equivalence; constraint solving; SAT; SMT;\n theorem-prover handoff where appropriate.\n\nPipeline:\n Premises + Query\n → Logical Formalization\n → Consistency / well-formedness check\n → Select calculus / solver\n → Forward/backward reasoning and/or proof search\n → Proof / refutation / terminal status\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-CFCB2666D1 — DeductionResult..\nSemantics:\n DEDUCED = query follows in the declared formal system.\n REFUTED = negation of query follows in the declared formal system.\n NOT_DEDUCED = permitted only when the declared fragment/procedure is complete\n for the question and establishes non-entailment.\n INVALID = malformed/inconsistent formalization under the declared rules.\n UNKNOWN = timeout, undecidable case, incomplete calculus, missing assumptions,\n resource exhaustion or unresolved formalization.\n\nNo proof found ≠ NOT_DEDUCED in a generic bounded/incomplete reasoning system. DEDUCED is logical consequence\nconditional on premises; it is not empirical truth. Deduction cannot amplify the epistemic status of uncertain premises\nmerely by being valid.\n\n50.8 EMPIRICAL INDUCTION ENGINE\n\nInduce(\n observations: Set<Observation>,\n hypothesis_space: HypothesisSpace,\n induction_profile: InductionProfile\n) → InductionResult\n\nSupported profiles:\n enumerative induction; statistical generalization; Bayesian induction;\n pattern induction; trend inference; population inference;\n causal induction; hypothesis generalization.\n\nPipeline:\n Observations\n → quality/provenance/independence checks\n → candidate pattern generation\n → support + contradiction analysis\n → sampling/selection-bias analysis\n → uncertainty estimation\n → out-of-distribution analysis\n → scope determination\n → InductionResult\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-3B90D63E61 — InductionProfile..\nNo universal confidence formula is mandated. The historical simple profile support/(support+contradiction) is only a\nsuitable special case for narrowly defined binary settings. General induction is governed by the Mathematical\nRepresentation Policy and domain-appropriate estimators.\n\nA counterexample is not automatic rejection unless the hypothesis claims universal, exceptionless behavior. Statistical\nlaws may legitimately contain expected exceptions.\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-BD8B56830E — InductionResult..\nInferenceMeasure may represent Probability, Distribution, Interval, LogOdds, LogEvidence, Confidence, SupportMeasure or\nanother semantically declared measure. Representation ≠ semantic meaning. Empirical induction produces\nsupport/uncertainty, never formal necessity.\n\n50.9 MATHEMATICAL INDUCTION & FORMAL PROOF STRATEGY REGISTRY\n\nMathematical induction is deductive formal proof, not empirical induction.\n\nFlow:\n Engine.Reason selects ProofStrategy\n → Domain.Mathematics supplies mathematical structures/induction principles\n → Engine.Proof machine-checks proof obligations\n → ProofCertificate\n\nProofStrategy leaf strategies currently include:\n\nClassical logical:\n DIRECT\n CONTRAPOSITIVE\n CONTRADICTION\n CASE_ANALYSIS\n EXISTENCE\n UNIQUENESS\n\nComputational / algebraic:\n EQUATIONAL\n ALGEBRAIC\n RECURSIVE\n FIXED_POINT\n\nMathematical induction:\n INDUCTION_WEAK / ORDINARY\n INDUCTION_STRONG / COMPLETE\n INDUCTION_STRUCTURAL\n INDUCTION_WELL_FOUNDED\n INDUCTION_COURSE_OF_VALUES\n INDUCTION_MUTUAL\n INDUCTION_NESTED\n INDUCTION_LEXICOGRAPHIC\n INDUCTION_TRANSFINITE\n\nCoinduction:\n COINDUCTION_BISIMULATION\n COINDUCTION_GREATEST_FIXED_POINT\n\nAutomated:\n AUTOMATED_SAT\n AUTOMATED_SMT\n THEOREM_PROVER\n\nOrdinary induction:\n P(0) ∧ (P(n) → P(n+1)) ⇒ ∀n∈ℕ, P(n)\n\nStrong induction:\n (∀k≤n, P(k)) → P(n+1), together with the required base condition(s).\n\nStructural induction applies to recursively generated structures including:\n GSL ASTs; proof terms; expression trees; recursive schemas;\n dependency structures; process structures; branch histories.\n\nWell-founded induction generalizes to a declared relation with no infinite descending chain. Transfinite induction\napplies over a declared well-order. Coinduction establishes properties of potentially infinite/co-recursive structures\nthrough bisimulation/greatest-fixed-point reasoning.\n\nA successful mathematical induction proof yields FORMAL PROVEN status relative to the declared axioms, definitions,\ninduction principle and formal system after Proof checks. It does not by itself establish that empirical premises/models\nabout the physical world are true.\n\n50.10 ABDUCTION\n\nObservation\n → candidate explanatory hypotheses\n → assumption + scope analysis\n → explanatory comparison\n → falsification attempts\n → best current candidate(s)\n\nABDUCTED = best available explanatory candidate under the declared comparison.\nIt never means TRUE, PROVEN or VERIFIED merely because it explains the observation.\n\n50.11 ARGUMENTATION\n\nClaim\n├── supports\n├── attacks\n├── rebuttals\n├── defeaters\n└── defenses\n\nSupported semantics include Dung Grounded, Preferred and Stable semantics.\nARGUED = accepted/surviving under the declared argumentation framework.\nARGUED ≠ FACT.\n\n50.12 ANALOGICAL REASONING\n\nSource system\n → structural mapping\n → candidate correspondence\n → difference analysis\n → applicability check\n → transferred hypothesis\n\nStructural similarity ≠ proof. Analogical transfer creates a candidate relation requiring independent validation.\n\n50.13 DEFAULT / NON-MONOTONIC REASONING\n\nSupports defeasible rules and explicit exceptions, e.g.:\n Bird(x) normally → Flies(x)\n Penguin(x) → exception → ¬Flies(x)\n\nConclusions carry supporting defaults, checked exceptions, defeaters, retraction conditions and validity scope. New\nevidence may legitimately retract a previous conclusion; this is not an error in non-monotonic reasoning.\n\n50.14 PROBABILISTIC / BAYESIAN REASONING\n\nGeneral form:\n prior state + evidence + dependency structure → posterior state\n\nFor Bayesian probability semantics:\n P(H|E) = P(E|H)·P(H)/P(E)\n\nConstraints:\n - probability semantics must actually apply;\n - Mathematical Representation Policy controls representation;\n - Probability, LogOdds, LogEvidence, Interval, Distribution, Tensor, etc.\n are representations/types with declared semantics, not interchangeable universal scores;\n - correlated evidence cannot be treated as independent merely because it came from\n multiple records/models/sources.\n\n50.15 CAUSAL REASONING\n\nAssociation\n → causal hypothesis\n → SCM / causal graph\n → assumption validation\n → intervention reasoning\n → causal estimate\n\nSupports intervention semantics such as P(Y | do(X=x)). Causal claims MUST identify causal structure, confounders,\nassumptions, identification method, intervention semantics and scope appropriate to the claim. Correlation alone cannot\ncreate causal status.\n\n50.16 COUNTERFACTUAL REASONING\n\nObserved world + causal/model state + alternative intervention\n → counterfactual trajectory.\n\nDirectly supports Historical Counterfactual Optimization, Prediction, Evolution, Decision analysis and Incident\nreconstruction. Counterfactual conclusions inherit the uncertainty/limitations of the model from which they are\ngenerated.\n\n50.17 TEMPORAL & SPATIAL REASONING\n\nTemporal:\n before/after; during; since; until; always; eventually; valid-at; expired-at;\n superseded-at; causal ordering; temporal obligations.\n\nSpatial:\n inside/outside; containment; adjacency; intersection; distance; direction;\n route; reachability; coordinate transformation; topological relation.\n\nThese consume existing TIME and SPACE semantics and do not create new ontology.\n\n50.18 ADVERSARIAL / FALSIFICATION REASONING\n\nCandidate\n → assume candidate may be wrong\n → attack assumptions/boundary conditions/evidence/composition\n → search counterexamples\n → test adversarial variants.\n\nSurvival means only NO COUNTEREXAMPLE FOUND WITHIN DECLARED SEARCH, never proof.\n\n50.19 DECISION REASONING\n\nBeliefs + candidate actions + predicted consequences + values + risks + constraints + resources\n → Recommendation.\n\nPossible form:\n a* = argmax_a EU(a)\nsubject to Constitution, Rights, Safety/K0P, Authority, Law, Policy, Resources and explicit epistemic uncertainty.\n\nRecommendation ≠ Authorization.\n\n50.20 ETHICAL / NORMATIVE REASONING\n\nFACT = what evidence indicates is.\nVALUE = what is valued/preferred.\nRIGHT = protected constitutional constraint.\nLAW = governed legal requirement.\nPOLICY = operational rule.\nDECISION = recommended action.\n\nIS ⇏ OUGHT without an explicit normative premise. Reasoning may relate these categories but may not silently convert one\ninto another.\n\n50.21 GAME-THEORETIC / MULTI-AGENT REASONING\n\nModels agents, strategies, information, beliefs, payoffs, incentives, coalitions, adversaries, equilibria, coordination\nand mechanism design. Relevant to Economy, Governance, Security, Agent, Evolution and Earth-branch coordination. An\nequilibrium is strategic stability under assumptions; it does not establish ethical legitimacy.\n\n50.22 OPTIMIZATION REASONING\n\nObjective + decision variables + feasible set + constraints + uncertainty + baseline\n → candidate optimum / Pareto set.\n\nWhere applicable, mandatory comparison includes Current_System, DO_NOTHING and candidate alternatives. Optimal ≠ Safe.\nOptimal ≠ True. Optimal ≠ Authorized.\n\n50.23 PLANNING REASONING\n\nCurrent State → Goal → candidate actions → preconditions/effects\n → temporal/resource constraints → prediction → contingencies → Plan.\n\nSupports classical, hierarchical, temporal, contingent, resource-constrained and multi-agent planning. Execution remains\nCapability.Compute.Execution, subject to authority/safety.\n\n50.24 EXPLANATORY REASONING\n\nPrediction asks: What happens? Explanation asks: Why did it happen?\n\nObserved outcome\n → causal/procedural lineage\n → relevant mechanism\n → assumptions + alternatives\n → ExplanationArtifact.\n\nEngine.Reason determines explanatory structure; Engine.Explanation renders it for humans.\n\n50.25 THEORY REASONING — GENERAL THEORY ENGINE\n\nEngine.Reason supports first-class:\n theory discovery; theory invention; retrieval; formalization; applicability;\n comparison; falsification; composition; specialization; generalization;\n contradiction; equivalence; approximation; supersession; dependency;\n revalidation; selection; retirement.\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-72F1762E05 — TheorySignature..\nTheory operation ownership:\n Discovery/Invention → Engine.Research + Engine.Reason, producing candidate theories.\n Retrieval → Engine.Search.\n Applicability/Comparison → Engine.Reason.\n Falsification → Engine.Reason + Engine.Research where experiments are needed.\n Composition → Engine.Reason, compatibility required.\n Contradiction/Equivalence→ Engine.Reason + Engine.Proof where formalizable.\n Dependency → Engine.Dependency.\n Revalidation → Engine.Reason + Capability.Knowledge + Continuous Epistemic Revalidation.\n Supersession → Engine.Reason proposal + Capability.Knowledge lineage + normal GTF governance.\n\nTheory invention creates a CANDIDATE theory, never established truth.\n\n50.26 THEORY STATUS SYSTEM\n\nTheory status is separate from inference status.\nHigh-level lifecycle/status vocabulary:\n ESTABLISHED | DERIVED | PROPOSED | EXPERIMENTAL | SPECULATIVE | REJECTED\n\nA theory separately carries formal_status, empirical_status, application_status, scope, freshness and provenance.\n\"Deduced using Theory X\" does not imply \"Theory X is empirically correct.\"\n\n50.27 META-REASONING\n\nMeta-reasoning decides how Garden should reason.\n\nIt asks:\n - Which reasoning modes apply?\n - Which theories are relevant/applicable?\n - How deep should reasoning go?\n - Which models/tools/solvers are appropriate?\n - Which modes can safely compose?\n - What would falsify the result?\n - What evidence is missing?\n - When should reasoning stop, defer or escalate?\n\nTriggers include novelty, UNKNOWN/CONFLICTED outcomes, resource pressure, mode disagreement, changed theory\ndependencies, and Safety/Constitution requirements.\n\nExamples:\n Arithmetic → Deduction.\n Mathematical theorem → Deduction + Formal Proof + mathematical induction if suitable.\n Clinical causal query → Causal + Bayesian + Evidence + Counterfactual + Adversarial.\n Engineering design → Deduction + Modeling + Optimization + Prediction + Counterfactual + Adversarial verification.\n Unknown phenomenon → Abduction + Empirical Induction + Theory Discovery + Experiment Design.\n Conflicting legal case → Deduction + Argumentation + Temporal + Ethical/Normative reasoning.\n\nOutput: ReasoningPlan + ReasoningTrace.\n\n50.28 MODE COMPOSITION\n\nModes are composable but cannot silently amplify each other.\n\nExample:\n Observation\n → Abduction\n → Candidate Hypothesis\n → Empirical Induction\n → Supported Pattern\n → Causal Analysis\n → Candidate SCM\n → Deduction\n → Conditional consequence.\n\nFormal necessity conditional on uncertain premises ≠ unconditional certainty. If valid modes materially disagree, status\nremains CONFLICTED or UNKNOWN until resolved. No averaging merely to force a single answer.\n\nReason Composition Contract:\nTheories/modes composed by Engine.Reason MUST provide compatible UncertaintyPropagationProfile semantics. If required\nprofiles are absent, incompatible or outside declared error bounds, composition status MUST be UNKNOWN and MUST NOT be\npromoted as verified.\n\n50.29 INFERENCE STATUS ≠ EPISTEMIC STATUS\n\nInferenceStatus =\n DEDUCED | REFUTED | NOT_DEDUCED |\n INDUCED_SUPPORTED | INDUCED_WEAK | INDUCED_CONTRADICTED |\n ABDUCTED | ARGUED | INVALID | UNKNOWN\n\nEpistemicStatus remains orthogonal, including:\n PROVEN | VERIFIED | SUPPORTED | UNVERIFIED | CONTRADICTED | RETRACTED | UNKNOWN/subtypes.\n\nExample:\n InferenceStatus = DEDUCED\n EpistemicStatus = SUPPORTED\nbecause the inference is formally valid but an empirical premise is only SUPPORTED.\n\n50.30 UNIVERSAL INFERENCE RESULT\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-76AE49974C — InferenceResult..\n50.31 REASONING PIPELINE — UPA PROFILE\n\nThe current normalized process:\n FORMALIZE → RETRIEVE → FALSIFY → COMPOSE → CHECK → MANAGE → REASON\nis retained as lineage but normalized as a Universal Process Algebra profile:\n\nPROBLEM\n → FORMALIZE\n → CLASSIFY\n → RETRIEVE theories/evidence\n → SELECT reasoning modes\n → BUILD ReasoningPlan\n → EXECUTE modes\n → FALSIFY / CHALLENGE\n → COMPOSE compatible results\n → VERIFY formal obligations\n → PROPAGATE uncertainty\n → CHECK epistemic/scope/dependency status\n → TERMINATE / DEFER / ESCALATE\n → InferenceResult\n → ClaimValidationPlan where promotion/consequential use is intended\n → Proof / Research / Simulation-Test / Legal-Authority / Human-Review paths as required\n → Explain / Recommend / ResearchGap / UNKNOWN.\n\n50.31.1 REASONING-TO-VALIDATION ROUTER\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-6CC4CB8E94 — ClaimValidationPlan.\nEvery inference or candidate claim intended for promotion, consequential recommendation or action receives a typed\nClaimValidationPlan. Routing is many-to-many rather than a false Proof-versus-Research binary:\n\n  FORMAL            → Engine.Proof checks entailment, proof obligations or model consistency.\n  EMPIRICAL         → Engine.Research acquires/tests observations and evidence.\n  BOTH              → Formal and empirical paths are independently required; neither substitutes for the other.\n  SIMULATION_TEST   → Qualified simulation, benchmark, property test or domain validation.\n  LEGAL_AUTHORITY   → Law/Policy/Constitution resolves applicability and authorization, not empirical truth.\n  HUMAN_REVIEW      → Qualified human/domain/governance review where judgment or legitimate authority is required.\n  UNROUTABLE_UNKNOWN→ Clarify, quarantine, defer or escalate; never silently promote.\n\nRouting predicates consume claim kind, intended use/promotion, assumptions, falsifiability/testability, formalizability,\ndomain, risk, authority, evidence gap, resources and context. A plan may select several paths with dependency order,\nacceptance criteria, terminal behavior and reconciliation rules. Engine.Reason owns routing; each destination retains\nits own epistemic and authority boundary.\nInvariant references: VAL-ROUTE-001..006.\n\n50.32 CONTINUOUS REVALIDATION / THEORY DEPENDENCY INTEGRATION\n\nNew evidence or a changed upstream theory triggers:\n Continuous Epistemic Revalidation\n → affected claims/theories discovered\n → TheoryDependencyGraph marks dependent theories/inferences REVALIDATION_REQUIRED\n → affected cached InferenceResults invalidated\n → applicable modes re-run\n → CONFIRMED / STRENGTHENED / WEAKENED / REFINED / CONTRADICTED / UNKNOWN.\n\nInvalidation is impact-indexed, incremental and priority-bounded. A REFUTED upstream theory immediately quarantines\nconsequential affected outputs, but recomputation proceeds in batches/lazily from immutable snapshots rather than\nsynchronously traversing the entire graph or crashing active Runtime contexts. Runtime may use only an unaffected\nlast-valid binding or enter a declared conservative degradation.\n\nReasoning is therefore living, dependency-aware and DesignEpoch-bound.\n\n50.33 EARTH CANONICAL BRANCH INTEGRATION\n\nLocal branch theory/proof/observation\n → BranchChangeManifest\n → Earth Frontier\n → Engine.Reason: comparison, deduction, induction, analogy, causal/counterfactual analysis,\n adversarial challenge and discriminating-evidence identification\n → Research/Proof\n → MERGE | REMAIN_LOCAL | REJECT | UNRESOLVED.\n\nConvergence/votes/popularity may nominate a candidate but cannot create truth.\n\n50.34 INVARIANT REFERENCES — REASONING FAMILY\n\nCanonical definitions: Annexure A.\nInvariant references: RSN-001..010, RSN-011..014 RESERVED, RSN-015..021, INF-001..024.\n50.35 DEPENDENCIES & MATHEMATICAL BINDING\n\nRead:\n GardenCore.Semantics.GSL, Domain.Mathematics, Engine.Proof, Capability.Trust.Safety, Capability.Knowledge,\n HumanCore.Constitution,\n Capability.State.TimeService, Capability.Authority.Governance, Engine.Search, Engine.Evolve, Engine.Explanation,\n Engine.Dependency,\n Engine.Policy, Engine.Research, Domain.Society.Economics, HumanCore.DelegatedAgent.\nWrite:\n Capability.State.EventService, Capability.Knowledge, and governed Research/Evolution requests.\n\nMath families used include:\n M0 proof theory, formal logic, Hoare/type systems;\n M1 graph/order/algebra/category/refinement/concurrency;\n M3 probability/statistics/information/causal inference/decision/game theory;\n M4 optimization/complexity/solver selection.\n\nRelevant proof obligations include P2, P3, P5, P6, P7a/P7b, P8, P12, P14, P18 and other obligations induced by the\nactual reasoning plan and ObligationGraph.\n\nEND OF DETAILED CAPABILITY / ENGINE / DOMAIN CONTRACTS\n\n6. Integer, real, temporal, quantified, exception-rich and open-world legal domains use\n typed symbolic constraints, partitions or bounded model checking rather than pretending they are a\n finite Boolean cube. Coverage, exclusions and solver completeness remain explicit.\n\nVerifyPatch(block, existing_blocks, global_invariants) -> PatchVerificationReport\n Checks syntax, types, satisfiability, deontic/temporal/jurisdictional interactions, constitutional\n constraints and affected tests. An UNSAT core is diagnostic evidence requiring interpretation; it does\n not mechanically prove that the proposed legal text is invalid in every legal reading.\n\nIncrementalCheck(changed_block) -> ImpactAnalysisReport\n Rechecks the transitive affected dependency closure plus all designated global invariants and\n common-mode constraints. Incrementality cannot hide a global effect outside the local closure.\n\nProof reference: LEGAL-SMT-P25.\n\nE.4 AUTOMATED LEGAL CI/CD\n\nOfficial source monitoring\n → content-addressed change detection\n → parsing\n → candidate formalization\n → ambiguity and trust assessment\n → dependency/global impact analysis\n → tests and SMT analysis\n → qualified human review where required\n → authority/governance gate\n → semantic commit\n → deployment/advisory release\n → continuous monitoring and revalidation.\n\nInvariant reference: EVO-014.\n\nE.5 FORMALIZATION TRUST\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-A89ED91715 — Predicate..\nVerificationLevel =\n V0_RAW_TEXT | V1_PARSED | V2_OPERATIONALIZED | V3_MACHINE_VERIFIED | V4_FORMALLY_PROVEN\n\nThe operationalization degree tau(p) estimates confidence in the declared translation/formalization under its evidence\nand review conditions. It is not the probability that the legal proposition is true, just, authoritative or\ncourt-adopted. Low tau triggers ambiguity preservation and review; human approval does not magically make a poor\nformalization true.\n\nInvariant reference: LANG-010.\n\nE.6 AI-ASSISTED FORMALIZATION\n\nAI systems may extract candidate blocks, citations, definitions, exceptions, temporal scopes and dependencies at scale.\nDeterministic parsers, cross-model checks, tests, SMT analysis, source comparison and qualified human experts review the\nrisk-appropriate subset.\n\nNo fixed AI/human percentage is normative. A measured ratio such as 95/5 may be tested as a pilot target, but review\nintensity follows ambiguity, novelty, legal consequence, jurisdiction, model performance and independent quality\nevidence. Human review is a responsibility and evidence channel, not automatic truth.\n\nE.7 HUMAN REVIEW PROFILE\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-7F6E0DFCAB — HumanReviewProfile..\nTimelines and quorums are configurable legal/governance parameters, not universal constants. If review expires,\nhigh-impact action remains blocked or enters the legally defined safe state; bounded low-risk continuity may use the\nintersection of clearly valid permissions. Emergency procedures must be fast enough for the emergency and cannot become\na permanent constitutional bypass.\n\nE.8 LEGAL-USE AND ADMISSIBILITY BOUNDARY\n\nGarden output is a traceable analysis, claim, model, test result or recommendation. It is not automatically law,\nevidence, admissible material, advocacy, a judgment or authority to act. Use in legal practice depends on current\napplicable law, institutional rules, competent professionals and the deciding tribunal.\n\nWhere external use is contemplated, Garden preserves source authenticity, chain of custody, reproducibility, method\ndisclosure, limitations, competing interpretations, human responsibility and challenge rights. Human authentication\nalone does not establish truth or admissibility.\n\nE.9 STAGED IMPLEMENTATION PROFILE\n\n1. Bounded pilot corpus: source ingestion, semantic version control, tests and reproducible solver traces.\n\n2. Larger coherent corpus: dependency graph, contradiction/gap analysis and qualified review operations.\n\n3. Institutional advisory twin: case-law/enforcement models, monitored use and external validation.\n\n4. Cross-domain legal twin: only after prior stages meet proof, accuracy, rights, security, governance and\n operational evidence gates.\n\nEach stage is advisory and bounded unless applicable law and independently validated governance authorize a stronger\nrole. Business/funding strategy is a separate non-normative project document.\n\nInvariant references: LEGAL-001..015, LEGAL-SMT-P25, LANG-010, EVO-014.\n\n8.9 GSL-BOOTSTRAP / TWO-FLEET / MODEL ROUTING\nVII-F — GSL-BOOTSTRAP / TWO-FLEET ARCHITECTURE\n\nF.1 GSL-BOOTSTRAP\n\nGarden may be bootstrapped from zero through an external heterogeneous LLM fleet. This is an internal lifecycle\nprotocol, not a new Garden component.\n\nSix phases: 1. Planning 2. Foundation 3. Building 4. Hardening 5. Handover 6. Operation\n\nThe external fleet builds and hardens the initial system. Handover requires Garden to demonstrate self-hosting\ncapabilities: it can verify itself, compile itself, route work through its authorized mechanisms, and perform the\ndeclared self-audit functions. After successful handover, the external fleet steps back.\n\nF.2 TWO-FLEET DISTINCTION\n\nBootstrap Fleet: External/pre-Garden heterogeneous fleet used before Garden is self-hosting.\n\nGarden Fleet: Internal/post-Garden authorized model/reasoning fleet used for operation, research, evolution,\nverification and routing subject to Garden authority.\n\nThe two roles are not interchangeable merely because both contain models.\n\nF.3 FLEETROUTER / MODELREGISTRY\n\nEngine.Reason internal state includes:\n\nModelRegistry: provider model_name version weights_hash runtime_version capability_score\n\nCapabilityScorer dimensions: reasoning_depth domain_expertise speed cost_efficiency reliability\n\nFleetRouter: Exploit: 90–95% Explore: 5–10% Exploration remains within the declared capability envelope.\n\nModel != Authority. Model selection occurs only from an authorized set; routing cannot create authority.\n\nEnsemble modes: SINGLE SEQUENTIAL PARALLEL ENSEMBLE DEBATE CROSS_VERIFY\n\nF.4 PHYSICAL WORLD MAPPING\n\nHome -> OS, Energy, Security, Agent Observe: temperature, motion, doors\nAct: lights, locks, HVAC\n\nCity -> Mobility, Energy, Governance Observe: traffic, air, power Act:\ntraffic lights, grid, transit\n\nBody -> Health, Safety Observe: biometrics Act: authorized\ndevices/reminders\n\nVehicle -> Mobility, Safety, Network Observe: GPS, LiDAR Act: brakes,\nsteering, throttle\n\nFactory -> Industry, Safety, Hardware Observe: machine sensors Act:\nPLCs, robotic arms\n\nGrid -> Energy, Safety, Distributed Observe: frequency, load Act:\nbreakers, generation\n\nEconomy -> Economy, Governance Observe: transactions, market Act:\nauthorized UBI/tax mechanisms\n\nEnvironment -> Governance, Carbon Observe: weather, climate Act:\ncontrols, conservation\n\nF.5 EPISTEMIC DEBT\n\nCapability.Knowledge contains:\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-083717EE84 — EpistemicDebt..\nIf total_debt_score exceeds the declared threshold, Engine.Evolve MUST trigger a mandatory ImprovementCycle through\nEngine.Research/Engine.Reason. DO_NOTHING remains a first-class candidate in that cycle.\n\nF.6 IMPROVEMENTFRONTIER DOMINANCE\n\nEvery candidate is compared against DO_NOTHING as the mandatory stability baseline. Dominance states: DOMINATES\nDOMINATED_BY\nINCOMPARABLE\n\nHard constraints are checked first. Infeasible candidates are rejected. A candidate cannot be accepted merely because it\nis better than another proposal; it must satisfy the DO_NOTHING comparison and the acceptance policy. Assessment, admissibility and certification\nremain distinct.\n\nF.8 NAMING / SCOPE CLARIFICATIONS\n\nReality Layer is explicitly the Reality layer and asks “What happened?”.\n\nDomain.Mathematics provides formal representations/operators for mathematical theories required by Garden operations; it\ndoes not claim to contain every mathematical theory.\n\nGardenCore.Semantics.GSL maps human languages to GSL through Context.LocaleCulture and the USI (Universal Semantic\nInterlingua) reference from GSL-UNIVERSAL.\n\n8.10 INCIDENT / CYBERSECURITY / DEFECT LEARNING\nThe lifecycle diagrams below are UPA profile projections; they do not create a second process engine.\nVII-G — INCIDENT, CYBERSECURITY, DEFECT LEARNING AND SELF-HARDENING\n\nG.1 GLOBAL SECURITY-LEARNING INVARIANT REFERENCES\n\nCanonical definitions: Annexure A.\nInvariant references: SEC-LEARN-001..010.\nDurable regression coverage uses content addressing, exact deduplication, semantic clustering with collision review and\nHot/Warm/Cold/Archive tiers. Evolution may improve its algorithms, but the modified mechanism\ncannot certify its own modification. TerminationContract bounds recursive self-improvement. OscillationDetection detects\nrepeated improvement/reversal cycles. Constitutional, hardware-trust, and safety roots remain outside the Evolution\nwritable set.\n\nG.16 PROACTIVE DEFENSIVE SCANNING\n\nVerified FailurePattern -> LearnedIndex -> Existing WorkPackages ->\nPending WorkPackages -> Runtime-relevant configurations -> Future\npatches.\n\nProactiveScan identifies: exact recurrence; structural variants; causal variants; equivalent state transitions;\nweakened/precondition-shifted versions; composition attacks.\n\nPositive matches trigger the applicable Security/Reason containment or verification pathway.\n\nG.17 REGRESSION PERMANENCE\n\nEvery verified significant incident generates: original replay + variant replays + legitimate counterexamples +\nregression tests + expected safety outcome.\n\nFuture versions are tested against the preserved regression set. Retirement requires governed review, explicit\nrationale, evidence the failure condition is no longer applicable, preserved provenance and a retirement audit.\n\nG.18 HUMAN/GOVERNANCE BOUNDARY\n\nAutomatic incident learning may detect, contain, reconstruct, classify, hypothesize, generate technical fixes, formally\nverify, replay, test, deploy within authorized technical boundaries, and learn generalized defensive patterns.\n\nIt SHALL NOT autonomously weaken constitutional rights, modify immutable constitutional roots, redefine human rights,\nalter fundamental governance authority, remove mandatory human review, or modify hardware trust roots outside authorized\nmechanisms.\n\nSuch changes escalate to Governance/Constitution.\n\nG.19 EMERGENCY OVERRIDE\n\nActive Threat -> Immediate Containment -> Evidence Preservation ->\nSafe-State / Emergency Mechanism -> Incident Reconstruction -> Root\nCause -> Corrective Research -> Verification -> Replay -> Deployment.\n\nEmergency containment may precede full verification only where an already- authorized emergency mechanism exists. The\nmechanism remains auditable and immutable within its authority boundary.\n\nG.20 FINAL LEARNING PROPERTY\n\nFAILURE -> DETECTION -> CONTAINMENT -> FORENSIC RECONSTRUCTION -> CAUSAL\nANALYSIS -> ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS -> GENERALIZED FAILURE PATTERN ->\nCANDIDATE REMEDIATION -> DO_NOTHING COMPARISON -> INDEPENDENT\nVERIFICATION -> HISTORICAL REPLAY -> ADVERSARIAL VARIANT TESTING ->\nPERMANENT REGRESSION -> CONTROLLED DEPLOYMENT -> POST-DEPLOYMENT\nVALIDATION -> DURABLE KNOWLEDGE -> PROACTIVE FUTURE DETECTION ->\nRECURSIVE AUDIT\n\nCore invariant: Garden SHALL learn from verified technical failures without allowing the failure, the diagnosis, the\nlearning mechanism, or the remediation mechanism to become self-authenticating authority.\n\n8.11 DESIGN EPOCH / BINDING / DRIFT / CONFORMANCE\nVII-H — DESIGN EPOCH, BINDING, DRIFT AND CONFORMANCE\n\nH.1 DESIGN EPOCH\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-C4CCD0ED87 — DesignEpoch.; SCHEMA-32C6E214AB — DesignBinding.;\n                   SCHEMA-146B6B8992 — EnvironmentCommitment.; SCHEMA-F3D094725B — KnowledgeSnapshot.;\n                   SCHEMA-1A2A6D825F — DesignEpochReadinessReport.\n\nDesignEpoch is Garden’s cryptographic constitutional time capsule: an immutable versioned snapshot of the complete\ncanonical design for a declared scope. It binds at least:\n  - every schema definition and schema-alias/migration record;\n  - every invariant and proof obligation;\n  - every registry entry and architecture-object identity/binding;\n  - the ten Core Objects and 24 Core Relations;\n  - Constitution and active Rights registry;\n  - compiler/CIR contracts and the normative GSL grammar/semantic version;\n  - capability/domain/profile definitions and their dependencies;\n  - acceptance evidence, verification receipts, authority and provenance roots.\n\nAn epoch becomes ACCEPTED only after all applicable gates succeed:\n  1. Integrity proof / registry-root consistency.\n  2. Constitutional and active-rights check.\n  3. Global invariant/proof-obligation analysis for the declared scope.\n  4. Interface/schema compatibility and required migration evidence.\n  5. Dependency closure/cycle/SCC analysis.\n  6. Independent frozen-verifier or equivalent independent verification.\n  7. Competent human/governance approval.\n\nDescribing these requirements does not self-certify the document. A human-readable master is only a DesignEpoch\ncandidate until machine receipts and independent acceptance exist.\n\nH.2 DESIGN BINDING\n\nEvery production artifact is permanently bound to the specific DesignEpoch it implements.\n\nDesignBinding contains: code hash, epoch reference, architecture_object_id, requirement/invariant/proof references,\nsafety/security constraints, environment commitment and verification status.\n\nCodeStatus lattice: COMPLIANT | STALE | INCONSISTENT | UNKNOWN |\nVERIFICATION_REQUIRED | BLOCKED\n\nH.3 DRIFT DETECTION — Engine.Search + Capability.Compute.Runtime\n\nRuntime periodically invokes Search to compare live code bindings with the latest accepted DesignEpoch.\n\nDrift Index: - inverted map: Epoch -> affected artifacts - delta index:\nBlueprint Hash <-> Live Binding Hash - priority queue ranked by blast\nradius, epistemic debt, safety/security criticality\n\nDetected STALE, INCONSISTENT or VERIFICATION_REQUIRED states emit auditable Events. Safety-critical drift escalates\nimmediately.\n\nH.4 IMPACT ANALYSIS / PROOF INVALIDATION — Engine.Proof\n\nWhen a new epoch is accepted, compute a Design Diff against the previous epoch. Impact Closure determines affected\nrequirements, invariants, architecture objects, interfaces, schemas, state machines, dependencies, assumptions, proof\nobligations,\nsafety/security constraints and deployed bindings.\n\nProofs whose assumptions, dependencies or interfaces changed become STALE and cannot be used until re-discharged against\nthe new epoch.\n\nH.5 RECURSIVE CONFORMANCE ENGINE — Engine.Evolve\n\nMandatory enforce_conformance loop: 1. Load latest accepted Epoch. 2. Scan live system for drift. 3. If drift empty,\nemit ConformanceCertificate and exit. 4. Run impact analysis. 5. Generate candidate patches, explicitly including\nDO_NOTHING. 6. For each candidate ranked by risk/reversibility: - adversarial falsification; - independent verification;\n- projected-state simulation; - Sandbox execution and global-conformance verification; - Canary execution and\nglobal-conformance verification; - atomic commit and post-commit verification. 7. On success, emit patch certificate and\nre-scan. 8. If all candidates fail or DO_NOTHING is justified, stop. 9. Oscillation/depth/resource-limit exceedance\nescalates to governance.\n\nRecursion is bounded by TerminationContract: depth, attempts and oscillation. Non-convergence blocks deployment and\nrequires human review.\n\nH.6 PATCH DEPENDENCY ORDER\n\nStrict order: 1. Trust roots & Constitution. 2. Schemas & types. 3. Interfaces & core dependencies. 4. Safety/security\nkernels. 5. Dependent implementations. 6. Integration & deployment artifacts.\n\nA dependent patch cannot be certified until prerequisite patch verification and commit are complete.\n\nH.7 EIGHT-LEVEL CONFORMANCE VERIFICATION\n\nAll levels must pass for global conformance: 1. Structural — architecture objects, interfaces, dependencies, schemas. 2.\nSemantic\n— state transitions, invariants, scope non-widening. 3. Safety — K0P barriers, fail-safe reachability. 4. Security —\nauthorization, trust roots, PQC, privilege boundaries. 5. Proof — discharged obligations, assumption freshness. 6.\nOperational — resources, latency, determinism, auditability. 7. Provenance — valid DesignBinding, full lineage trace. 8.\nGlobal Composition — cross-component blast radius, shared invariants.\n\ncheck_conformance(epoch, snapshot) -> PASS/FAIL + detailed violations.\n\nH.8 DEPLOYMENT GATE / EMERGENCY OVERRIDE — Capability.Compute.Execution\n\nUnrestricted deployment is rejected if status is BLOCKED, INCONSISTENT,\nUNKNOWN or VERIFICATION_REQUIRED.\n\nEmergency path is allowed only through Capability.Resilience.Emergency with explicit authorization, bounded\nscope/duration, immutable audit trail, Constitution/K0P preservation, mandatory post-emergency reconciliation and\nre-verification.\n\nAn override cannot permanently mark an artifact COMPLIANT.\n\nH.9 CONFORMANCE CERTIFICATE — Capability.Knowledge\n\nCertificate captures epoch, system snapshot, artifact-set hash and PASS/FAIL for all eight verification levels. It\nreferences adversarial review, independent verification, invalidated proofs and active exceptions.\n\nIt becomes invalid if: - DesignEpoch is superseded; - bound assumption/dependency/environment/source/compiler input\nchanges; - post-deployment verification fails.\n\nStatuses: FULL | CONDITIONAL | EXCEPTION | FAILED | PENDING\n\nH.10 CONFORMANCE EXCEPTION\n\nConformanceException is an explicit bounded waiver for specific artifacts or requirements. It requires justification,\nrisk assessment, compensating controls, expiry, independent review and explicit authority.\n\nIt cannot widen design scope, weaken constitutional roots, erase provenance or bypass independent verification\npermanently.\n\nH.11 PROVENANCE CHAIN\n\nEvery production artifact has an immutable trace: Requirement -> Design\n-> Epoch -> ArchitectureObject -> Implementation -> Dependency Set -> Proofs ->\nAdversarial Review -> Independent Verification -> Deployment -> Runtime\nState -> Conformance Certificate.\n\nBroken link -> UNKNOWN or VERIFICATION_REQUIRED -> unrestricted\ndeployment blocked until restored.\n\nH.12 SELF-CONFORMANCE OF CONFORMANCE MACHINERY\n\nThe following mechanisms themselves require valid DesignBindings and ConformanceCertificates: DesignEpoch registry;\nBinding registry; Drift detector; Impact analyzer; Patch generator; Adversarial verifier; Independent verifier;\nConformance checker; Deployment gate; Rollback mechanism; Certificate issuer.\n\nMeta-Evolution requires independent verification using a frozen/trusted baseline. The evolving mechanism cannot be its\nown sole judge.\n\nH.13 DCC FAMILY — GLOBAL CONFORMANCE INVARIANT REFERENCES\n\nCanonical definitions: Annexure A.\nInvariant references: DCC-001..036.\nH.14 TEN SEALING PRINCIPLES\n\n1. The latest accepted DesignEpoch is authoritative.\n\n2. No code is trusted merely because it was generated by Garden.\n\n3. The conformance machinery is itself subject to conformance.\n\n4. A design change propagates through impact analysis and proof\n invalidation.\n\n5. Local correctness never substitutes for global correctness.\n\n6. Every repair is adversarially reviewed and independently verified.\n\n7. Recursive repair is bounded and cannot recursively modify its own\n trust roots.\n\n8. DO_NOTHING remains a legitimate outcome.\n\n9. Exceptions are temporary, explicit, auditable and cannot silently\n weaken constitutional roots.\n\n10. Deployment is continuously rechecked after commitment.\n\nH.15 DESIGNEPOCH PROTECTION — “CONSTITUTIONAL TIME CAPSULE” VIEW\n\nNo silent drift\n Every production artifact binds to a specific accepted DesignEpoch. A relevant design/environment/knowledge change\n invalidates or re-evaluates the affected binding rather than silently changing meaning.\n\nNo self-certification\n The system/ mechanism proposing an epoch cannot be its sole independent verifier or certifier.\n\nNo retroactive rewriting\n Accepted DesignEpochs are immutable historical states. A change creates a successor epoch and explicit migration.\n\nGoverned evolution\n Epoch transition uses impact analysis, proof/evidence, migration, rollback/compensation and legitimate authority.\n\nTrust-root preservation\n Physical trust roots, K0P and constitutional roots remain outside ordinary Evolution’s writable authority.\n\nH.16 CURRENT DESIGNEPOCH VALIDATION CHECKLIST — HUMAN-SOURCE STATUS\n\nCURRENT MACHINE-CLOSURE GATES\nThe following are no longer hand-authored document tasks. They are mandatory generated/verification stages:\n\n  1. It escalates method strength only when uncertainty, consequence, novelty,\ndisagreement, expected information gain or verification failure requires it. Compute consumption is not treated as\nintelligence or evidence.\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-FE0A9B783C — ComputationContract.; SCHEMA-9544FD09C4 — ResearchValueEstimate..\nThe estimate prioritizes optional research, experiments, proof attempts, simulations and branches. It cannot suppress\nmandatory constitutional, safety, incident, proof, audit or revalidation work.\n\nAdaptive budget factors:\n uncertainty × consequence × novelty × disagreement × expected information gain.\n\nVerification ladder:\n\n cheapest plausible method\n → cheap independent checker\n → PASS at required assurance: stop\n → disagreement/uncertainty: deeper reasoning or broader models\n → stronger verifier\n → formal proof, experiment or governance boundary where required.\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-17BD8B5A15 — VerificationLadderReceipt..\nHard-invariant / learned-behavior separation\n\nHard invariants are enforced by deterministic, cryptographic, formal, hardware or otherwise independently verified\nmechanisms appropriate to the risk. Intelligence growth != human irrelevance. Human-scale communication remains permanently\navailable even if internal reasoning becomes vastly more complex.\n\nHuman-facing path:\n extreme internal complexity\n -> Engine.Explanation\n -> clear user-chosen language\n -> visual representation where useful\n -> UnderstandingRecord\n -> human choice/consent where required.\n\nNo \"trust the incomprehensible intelligence\" authority rule exists.\n\nOrdinary human civilization is a protected continuity state.
