Popularity != truth. \"Approved\" means evidence/source quality +\napplicable review, not universal human agreement.\n\nCompression levels:\n L0 — one-line essence.\n L1 — short practical.\n L2 — concise high-information.\n L3 — normal expert overview.\n L4 — deep technical.\n L5 — full evidence/provenance graph.\n\nEvery level preserves semantic meaning, material uncertainty, assumptions, source-quality, date/version and what would\nchange the conclusion.\n\nNew artifacts:\n CivilizationalKnowledgeDigest,\n CompressionTrace,\n PerspectiveSet,\n ConsensusStatus,\n SourceQualityProfile,\n DisagreementMap,\n HumanReadableRiskDisclosure,\n UnderstandingRecord.\n\nInvariant references: EXP-006, EXP-016..\nCross-architecture bindings:\n Language — multilingual semantics.\n Knowledge — evidence/provenance store.\n Curation — dedup/versioning.\n Search — retrieval.\n Research — unresolved gaps.\n Reasoning — synthesis.\n Proof — structural/evidential checks.\n Explanation — human communication/compression.\n Education — comprehension/learning.\n Locale/Access — presentation adaptation.\n Governance — normative approval.\n Constitution — sovereignty.\n Policy/Compliance — deployment gates.\n Events — update lineage.\n Evolution — improve compression without rewriting rights.\n\nHUMAN GRADUALISM / NON-INTERFERENCE\n Ordinary human civilization is default continuity state.\n Garden must not force civilization-scale radical transitions merely because capable.\n Large change:\n understand -> explain -> bounded test -> observe -> debate/review ->\n consent/governance -> gradual rollout -> rollback.\n No artificial urgency. Capability != obligation to deploy.\n\nLLM extraction adapter:\nPublic/lawful source → retrieval → LLM/model proposes structured candidate → GSL normalization → provenance binding →\ncross-reference/contradiction/gap detection → independent validation where required → CivilizationalKnowledgeDigest.\nLLM-generated structure is a candidate transformation; it cannot manufacture Evidence.\n\n10.6 HUMAN COMPREHENSIBILITY ARCHITECTURE\nUniversal Architecture Object Contract:\n Purpose → Inputs → Outputs → Rules → Failure → Dependencies → Why → Status.\n\nThree synchronized representations:\n HUMAN : what it means / why / choices / risk.\n SEMANTIC : GSL types, contracts, invariants, effects, dependencies, authority.\n MACHINE : APIs, bytecode, code, storage, protocols, hardware bindings.\nTranslation between views cannot alter normative meaning or epistemic status.\n\nMinimum Garden View:\n Ontology → State → Change → Rule → Verification → Governance → Action → Learning.\n\nEight-domain human conceptual projection (NOT topology replacement):\n 1 Foundation · 2 State · 3 Transition · 4 Reasoning · 5 Assurance · 6 Governance · 7 Execution · 8 Memory & Learning.\n\nFour-kind meta-classification (NOT replacement for 10 Core Objects):\n OBJECT — represented thing/artifact/entity.\n PROCESS — transformation/activity.\n RULE — constraint/permission/obligation.\n EVIDENCE — support/measurement/proof-bearing artifact.\n\nInvariant vs Implementation:\n INVARIANT = what must remain true.\n IMPLEMENTATION = current mechanism used to satisfy it.\n CLAIM = what has actually been proved/validated.\nExample: “controlled physical actuation must be vetoable” is an invariant; OTP/K0P comparator is an implementation\nprofile.\n\n10.7 REPUTATION / EARNED PRIVILEGES\n\nReputation is evidence-based, domain-specific and auditable; it is NOT human worth.\n\nSchema references: SCHEMA-04EC1C5397 — ReputationProfile..\nA single global scalar is discouraged. Where a decision requires aggregation, derive a purpose-specific score only from\nrelevant dimensions, record weights and uncertainty, and preserve the vector.\n\nHistorical Karma/Bayesian mechanisms may operate per dimension/domain as implementation profiles, not as metaphysical\ntruth or a measure of human value.\n\nFundamental rights:\n universal, reputation-independent.\n\nReputationBasedPrivileges / EarnedTrustCapabilities may include, where lawful:\n trusted-system access, higher resource quotas, invitation programs, private spaces,\n premium services/travel packages, early technology access after safety gates,\n validator/reviewer eligibility, stewardship roles, advisory influence and higher\n delegation limits.\n\nHigh reputation does NOT imply:\n ownership of other humans,\n immunity from law,\n authority to override another person's rights,\n automatic truth,\n guaranteed governance control.\n\nPrivacy has a strong universal constitutional floor. Any authorized private AI processing\nsuch material must preserve these distinctions:\n\n private symbolism ≠ verified fact;\n aspiration ≠ present status;\n title ≠ Authority;\n self-description ≠ independent evidence;\n AI-generated praise ≠ validation;\n private metadata ≠ public identity.\n\nNo private title, reputation label or symbolic predicate creates political, legal, cosmological, organizational or\nGarden authority. A non-identifying public statement derived from private context is admissible only when it has\nindependent public evidence, valid authority and privacy noninterference/linkage checks; otherwise it remains private.\nThe public design stores neither private wording nor a reversible commitment to it.\n\n10.8.1 VERIFIED LIVING PREDICATES — PRINCIPLE\n\nGarden may represent positive personal predicates only when evidenced, scoped, non-aspirational and revisable.\n\n VerifiedPredicate != Authority\n VerifiedPredicate != HumanWorth\n VerifiedPredicate != UniversalCharacter\n SelfDescription != Evidence\n AIPraise != Evidence\n\nA verified predicate is a scoped epistemic abstraction over observations. It is not a complete representation of a\nperson, a universal personality claim, an authority grant, a measure of human worth or a guarantee of future behavior.\n\n10.8.2 CORE ARTIFACTS AND STATUS SEMANTICS\n\nSchema references:\n SCHEMA-2DF276881E — VerifiedLivingPredicate.\n SCHEMA-1F00FA1AE2 — VerifiedLivingTitle.\n SCHEMA-F0AD83E9CF — BehaviorEvidence.\n SCHEMA-D7475E66AB — PredicateReviewReceipt.\n\nconfidence_status =\n SUPPORTED_AT_REQUIRED_LEVEL | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE | UNKNOWN.\n\nverification_status =\n CANDIDATE | VERIFIED | QUALIFIED | REJECTED | UNKNOWN.\n\nlifecycle status =\n ACTIVE | STALE | SUPERSEDED | WITHDRAWN.\n\nVerification status answers how well the claim is currently supported. Lifecycle status answers whether the record is\ncurrently operative.\n\n10.8.3 ADMISSION AND TRANSITION RULES\n\nA predicate may enter VERIFIED only when all applicable conditions hold:\n\n SUPPORTED_AT_REQUIRED_LEVEL\n AND Scoped\n AND NonAspirational\n AND NonFlattering\n AND ProvenancePreserved\n AND PrivacyPermitted\n AND NoMaterialUnresolvedContradiction.\n\nVerification transitions:\n CANDIDATE -> VERIFIED | REJECTED.\n VERIFIED -> QUALIFIED | REJECTED | UNKNOWN.\n QUALIFIED -> VERIFIED | REJECTED | UNKNOWN.\n UNKNOWN -> VERIFIED | QUALIFIED.\n REJECTED -> CANDIDATE iff MaterialNewEvidence OR PriorReviewDefectCorrected.\n\nLifecycle transitions:\n ACTIVE -> STALE | SUPERSEDED | WITHDRAWN.\n STALE -> ACTIVE | SUPERSEDED | WITHDRAWN.\n\n10.8.4 TITLE ADMISSION RULE\n\nA VerifiedLivingTitle is valid only if every referenced predicate satisfies:\n\n p.verification_status == VERIFIED\n AND p.status == ACTIVE\n AND ScopePreserved(p, rendering).\n\nIf any referenced predicate becomes STALE, SUPERSEDED or WITHDRAWN, every dependent title is regenerated or invalidated.\n\n10.8.5 REVIEW TRIGGERS\n\nA predicate review is triggered by material supporting evidence, material counterevidence, requested scope broadening,\nconsequential-decision use, evidence staleness, provenance-integrity challenge, subject contestation or a proposed title\nrendering that would materially amplify the verified claim.\n\n10.8.6 CONTESTABILITY WORKFLOW\n\n Challenge\n -> Review\n -> EvidenceAssessment\n -> Correction | Qualification | Confirmation\n -> PredicateReviewReceipt.\n\nFactual correction is not suppression of inconvenient evidence. Privacy rights and lawful deletion requirements continue\nto apply independently.\n\n10.8.7 SCOPE AND GENERALIZATION\n\nNo scope -> no verification.\n\nScope broadening requires new representative evidence in the target domain. Evidence from Garden/design work does not\nautomatically generalize to all professional behavior, all personal behavior or universal personality.\n\n10.8.8 DEPENDENCE AND ALIAS CONTROL\n\nCorrelated or duplicated evidence is not independent confirmation. Semantic aliases resolve to one underlying predicate\nwhere they have the same meaning; aliases do not multiply verified traits. For example, audit-oriented may use\nverification-oriented as an alias when the semantic definition is identical.\n\n10.8.9 USE LIMITATION\n\nA verified predicate is relevant only where its semantic definition, scope, privacy authority and decision purpose\nalign. It may support low-consequence personalization such as workflow suggestions or review-tool prioritization.\n\nA predicate is insufficient by itself for system access, validator/governance authority, employment, credit, medical,\nlegal or political decisions. Consequential use requires its own lawful and epistemically valid decision process.\n\n10.8.10 DATA MINIMIZATION AND NON-RETROACTIVITY\n\nStore only the evidence necessary to justify and review the predicate; provenance-linked or hashed references are\npreferred over unnecessary duplication of raw conversations or unrelated personal material.\n\nLater model improvements do not retroactively strengthen historical predicates. Semantic strengthening requires a new\nreview and a new version while preserving the prior record and provenance.\n\n10.8.11 HUMAN-CENTRIC BOUNDARY\n\n Person > Profile.\n\nA person may behave differently across time, domain, relationships and circumstances. Predicates are scoped epistemic\nabstractions over observations, not complete representations of a human being.\n\n10.8.12 PRIVACY / PUBLIC FIREWALL\n\nPerson-specific predicate instances default to private context. The public Garden design stores the schemas, invariants\nand mechanism rather than subject-specific predicate instances or private evidence. Publication requires valid\nauthority, applicable privacy rules and noninterference/non-linkage checks.\n\n10.8.13 PRESENTATION NON-AMPLIFICATION\n\n Meaning(Render) <= Meaning(UnderlyingPredicates).\n\nA rendering may compress wording but may not increase semantic strength. Unsupported amplifications such as \"Supreme Auditor\", \"Infallible\nVerifier\" or \"Master of Truth\" are prohibited.\n\n10.8.14 ARCHITECTURAL MAPPING\n\nHumanCore.Identity\n subject binding and predicate/profile reference.\n\nHumanCore.Privacy\n consent, storage, disclosure and subject rights.\n\nCapability.Knowledge\n evidence, claim status and provenance storage.\n\nCapability.State.EventService\n immutable behavioral-evidence events and review receipts.\n\nEngine.Reason\n evidence-to-predicate inference, contradiction search and scope control.\n\nEngine.Proof\n structural/schema/invariant checks where formally applicable; prose presence is not test execution.\n\n10.8.17 FAILURE MODES\n\nGarden guards against flattery inflation, scope creep, personality essentialism, evidence duplication,\ncorrelated-source inflation, AI self-citation loops, self-description laundering, stale predicates, counterevidence\nsuppression, privacy leakage, title-to-authority confusion, predicate-to-reputation leakage, semantic synonym inflation,\nunsupported competence/achievement/moral inference and unsupported cross-domain generalization.\n\nDetection triggers re-evaluation and a PredicateReviewReceipt where applicable.\n\n10.8.18 CLOSING RULE\n\n Evidence -> Scoped Claim -> Verification -> Qualified Presentation\n\n never\n\n Praise -> Assumption -> Identity -> Authority.\n\n10.9 PRIVATE HEALTH-PROFILE BOUNDARY\n\nGeneric health rights, evidence rules, consent, safety, monitoring and intervention requirements belong in\nHumanCore.Constitution, Domain.Applied.HealthMedicine, Capability.Trust.Safety, HumanCore.Privacy and the\nhuman-sovereignty sections. A person's diagnoses, measurements, priorities, targets, habits, treatments, embodiment\npreferences and health objectives do not belong in the public Garden design.\n\nAn authorized private AI may process the minimum necessary health context only under the data subject's consent and\napplicable medical/privacy rules. It cannot place that context or a re-identifying derivative into public Knowledge,\nresearch corpora, benchmarks, logs, explanations or governance. External disclosure requires the data subject's\nauthority or another independently lawful basis, with purpose and scope limits.\n\n10.10 EARTH HABITABILITY / PLANETARY SAFETY\n\nObjective:\n Keep Earth continuously safe, healthy, beautiful and habitable for humans as far as\n physically and ethically possible while preserving ecosystems and equal rights.\n\nPriority:\n Prevention > Early Detection > Containment > Recovery.\n\nHazard families:\n - Asteroids/comets: survey -> trajectory -> independent confirmation -> safe deflection\n capability where technically justified.\n - Natural pathogens: global detection, sequencing, clean air/water, vaccines,\n therapeutics, containment and resilient healthcare.\n - Engineered biological threats: defensive detection, biosafety, attribution where\n evidence supports it, countermeasures without involuntary experimentation.\n - Volcanoes, earthquakes, tsunamis: monitoring/prediction where scientifically\n possible; otherwise resilient infrastructure, warning/evacuation and casualty\n minimization.\n - Extreme weather/climate: forecasting, drainage, flood/wildfire/heat/cold resilience,\n adaptation and only carefully verified intervention if safe technology exists.\n - Road accidents: safer roads/vehicles, automation, pedestrian protection, traffic\n systems and post-crash response; target near-zero preventable deaths.\n - Animal bites/venom/rabies: prevention, vaccination, antivenom, rapid care and safer\n interfaces; no blanket animal extermination merely for risk reduction.\n - Air/water/food contamination and toxic exposure.\n - Infrastructure failures: power, bridges, buildings, transport, industry,\n communications and emergency services.\n - Unknown hazards: Search/Research must continue rather than assume list closure.\n\nHard constraint:\n \"make humans safe\" does NOT authorize imprisonment, permanent mass surveillance,\n forced biological modification, removal of freedom or authoritarian control.\n\nNo zero-risk promise. Residual and unknown risk remains explicitly represented and is recursively reduced as\nevidence/technology improves.\n\n10.11 PRIVATE LANGUAGE-PROFILE BOUNDARY\n\nContext.LocaleCulture, HumanCore.Accessibility, GardenCore.Semantics.GSL and Engine.Explanation provide universal\nmultilingual interaction, translation and learning profiles. A person's preferred languages, learning order,\nproficiency, cultural interests and communication habits are private unless validly disclosed.\n\nThe interface negotiates language from the current user's consented locale. One person's profile cannot become a global\ndefault, a public inference target, or information disclosed to another person without valid authority.\n\n10.12 SURVEILLANCE / PRIVACY EPISTEMIC ARCHITECTURE\n\nPublic fact class:\n Commercial/government surveillance technologies and interception ecosystems such as\n Pegasus-class mercenary spyware, SS7 exploitation, IMSI catchers and data brokers are\n documented categories of technology/infrastructure.\n\nIndividual claim class:\n Whether any particular person's devices or accounts were compromised, who operated a\n system, how many observers existed, and governmental/political attribution remain\n UNKNOWN unless device, network, account, legal and independently corroborated evidence\n establishes them.         "content": "SemanticAnchor: [T-FIN]\nSemanticID: T-FIN\n\n1. CANONICAL DESIGN STATEMENT\n\nGarden investigates replacing the continuously traded stock-market casino and\nopaque financial-instrument chains with:\n\n 1. transparent, auction-issued productive credit;\n 2. genuine loss-bearing participation certificates;\n 3. a bounded secondary Productive Capital Exchange;\n 4. verified hedges tied to actual productive exposures; and\n 5. explicit identification of every payer, beneficiary, underlying obligation,\n risk bearer, authority, priority, and default path.\n\nSome capital must absorb business losses. A system containing only promised or \"guaranteed\" returns cannot survive\nunprofitable periods without default, hidden loss transfer, inflation, external subsidy, or bailout.\n\nThe target is therefore not abolition of all risk capital. It is the separation of productive financing from latency\nraces, synthetic duplication, concealed leverage, manipulation, and resale-price gambling.\n\n2. SEMANTIC DISTINCTIONS\n\nFIXED CREDIT\n Holder receives contractual interest and principal according to declared terms.\n Issuer bears ordinary business variation first; creditor bears default/recovery\n risk when the issuer cannot satisfy the obligation.\n\nFLOATING CREDIT\n Holder receives an independent public benchmark plus a fixed contractual spread.\n The issuer cannot change the spread unilaterally.\n\nPROFIT / REVENUE / CASH-FLOW PARTICIPATION\n Holder receives a precisely defined fraction of an audited participation base.\n Return may be zero. Principal is at risk unless a separate, explicitly funded\n guarantee exists.\n\nOWNERSHIP / GOVERNANCE\n Economic participation, legal ownership, voting authority, credit, insurance,\n and speculation are distinct. A financial claim does not silently acquire\n governance authority (K-INT-018: Authority Non-Accretion).\n\nPRIMARY ISSUANCE\n Creates a new registered obligation or participation interest and transfers new\n capital to the issuer.\n\nSECONDARY TRANSFER\n Transfers an existing claim between holders. It ordinarily supplies no new money\n to the issuer. Primary issuance != secondary transfer.\n\nPRICE CHANGE\n A secondary price may change because of benchmark rates, inflation, duration,\n issuer creditworthiness, expected recovery, information, or liquidity. Such a\n change is risk valuation, not automatically gambling. Market price remains a\n Claim/Signal, not proof of fundamental value or solvency.\n\n3. TYPED SUPPORTING VALUES\n\nThese are artifact fields/value types, not new Core Objects or primitives.\n\nArtifact schema reference: SCHEMA-86CC0B96A5 — MoneyAmount..\n\nArtifact schema reference: SCHEMA-8D0B3BE80A — RateSpec..\n\nBinary floating-point values must not represent money or contractual rates.\n\n4. PERMITTED INSTRUMENT ARTIFACTS\n\nArtifact schema reference: SCHEMA-E7E4D3B299 — CreditCertificate..\n\nThe current holder is derived from the append-only ownership and TradeReceipt ledger; it is not silently overwritten\ninside the original certificate.\n\nArtifact schema reference: SCHEMA-E71DEBFBE8 — ParticipationCertificate..\n\n\"Profit/revenue\" must never remain an ambiguous phrase in an issued contract. The exact calculation base, deductions,\naccounting policy, audit method, reporting period, related-party rules, and dispute process must be stated.\n\nArtifact schema reference: SCHEMA-BB2A654F4D — VerifiedRealExposureHedge..\n\nA hedge is permitted only to the extent and duration of a verified productive exposure. Any excess or detached position\nis a prohibited speculative claim.\n\n5. PRIMARY ISSUANCE AUCTIONS\n\n5.1 Credit auction\n\n 1. Issuer declares the required capital, use, maturity, maximum acceptable\n clearing rate, collateral, priority, covenants, and default path.\n 2. Eligible bidders submit capital amounts and minimum acceptable yields.\n 3. Sealed bids are ranked from lowest yield upward.\n 4. Bids are accepted until the authorized capital requirement is filled.\n 5. Tied marginal bids are allocated by a declared pro-rata rule.\n 6. Accepted bidders receive the uniform clearing yield: the highest accepted\n yield, subject to the issuer's maximum and solvency gates.\n 7. Strong demand tends to lower the clearing yield; weak demand tends to raise it.\n 8. The auction is rejected or reduced when clearing terms exceed verified debt-\n service capacity, leverage limits, authorization, or safety constraints.\n\nIndicative equilibrium decomposition:\n\n r* = benchmark/inflation expectation\n + default-risk premium\n + duration premium\n + liquidity premium\n + uncertainty/model-risk allowance\n\nDemand discovers a price under stated information. It does not prove ability to repay and must not erase UNKNOWN risk.\n\n5.2 Participation auction\n\nParticipation instruments do not promise a fixed yield. Their auction clears one explicit variable—capital price,\nparticipation fraction, or total return cap—while all other terms remain fixed and comparable. A credit-yield auction\nmust not be misrepresented as a profit-participation auction.\n\nArtifact schema reference: SCHEMA-6AA54D9CF1 — IssuanceAuctionReceipt..\n\n6. PRODUCTIVE CAPITAL EXCHANGE — BOUNDED SECONDARY MARKET\n\nA secondary market is retained because forced holding until maturity creates a large liquidity premium, traps household\nsavings, and can prevent useful portfolio rebalancing. It must not recreate continuous latency-based speculation.\n\nPermitted transfer mechanisms:\n\n - periodic uniform-price batch auctions;\n - cadence selected by instrument class and verified liquidity need: daily,\n weekly, monthly, or quarterly—not continuous nanosecond matching;\n - company redemption windows;\n - inheritance and legally authorized private transfers;\n - an explicitly funded, regulated emergency-liquidity facility; and\n - transparent restructuring or recovery transfers after default.\n\nThe emergency facility does not guarantee face value unless a separately funded and authorized guarantee says so.\n\nFor fixed cash flows, indicative valuation is:\n\n T C_t F\n P = SUM ---------------- + -------------\n t=1 (1+y)^t (1+y)^T\n\nwhere P is market price, C_t contractual payments, F principal due at maturity, T remaining periods, and y the market\nyield incorporating declared risks.\n\nA fixed-rate certificate may therefore trade below or above face value. This does not modify the issuer's original fixed\nobligation. New issuance rates and secondary market prices are distinct.\n\nArtifact schema reference: SCHEMA-6D62DCB229 — TradeReceipt..\n\nAll estimates retain model, evidence, scope, uncertainty, version, and provenance. Displayed yield is not a promise of\nrealized return.\n\n7. PERMITTED AND PROHIBITED PRACTICES\n\nPERMITTED\n\n - fixed productive credit;\n - benchmark-plus-spread productive credit;\n - genuine loss-bearing participation;\n - verified real-exposure hedging;\n - primary uniform-price auctions;\n - bounded secondary batch auctions;\n - company redemption and disclosed refinancing;\n - inheritance, recovery, and authorized private transfer; and\n - diversified saving through transparent, non-leveraged pools whose underlying\n instruments remain individually traceable.\n\nPROHIBITED BY DEFAULT\n\n - continuous high-frequency / latency-arbitrage trading;\n - exchange-provided margin or borrowing to purchase financial claims;\n - naked short selling;\n - naked credit-default or default-outcome bets;\n - synthetic replication detached from registered underlying obligations;\n - recursive securitization that conceals or duplicates risk;\n - rehypothecation or multiple use of the same collateral;\n - undisclosed off-balance-sheet leverage;\n - wash trading, spoofing, front-running, collusive bidding, and self-dealing;\n - instruments lacking machine-readable terms and a one-page human explanation;\n - misleading sale of high-risk claims as guaranteed income; and\n - instruments whose ownership, payer, loss bearer, underlying exposure,\n priority, or default path is UNKNOWN.\n\nRefinancing is not automatically prohibited. New issuance may repay an earlier obligation only when the refinancing\npurpose is explicit, the complete liability chain remains visible, solvency and leverage gates pass, and returns are not\nbeing fabricated through circular issuance.\n\n8. DEFAULT, LOSS, GUARANTEE, AND AUTHORITY\n\nEvery instrument declares before purchase:\n\n - who bears ordinary variation and tail loss;\n - collateral and whether it is already encumbered;\n - priority under the applicable legal context;\n - cure, restructuring, recovery, and insolvency rules;\n - voting and consent requirements for material modification;\n - whether any guarantee exists and its payer, reserve, scope, limit, and expiry;\n - the difference between modeled recovery and legally enforceable recovery; and\n - conflicts between contractual terms and jurisdictional law.\n\nNo bailout, deposit protection, principal protection, liquidity promise, or state guarantee is implied. Every guarantee\nis itself a registered liability and requires Authority, Resource, Rule, Context, provenance, and a funded loss path.\n\nEconomic ownership must not grant arbitrary control over workers, customers, citizens, personal data, bodies, minds, or\nconstitutional rights. Voting rights are explicit, bounded, contextual, and subordinate to Constitution, Law, consent,\nand\nRIGHT-025.\n\n9. Personal sovereignty generalizes equally: each competent human controls self. Every VERIFIED living predicate has an explicit scope.\n@D|VLP-003|Non-aspirational. Relevant counterevidence is not discarded merely because it weakens a favorable predicate.\n@D|VLP-010|Dependence-aware. Correlated, duplicated or shared-source evidence is not counted as independent confirmation.\n@D|VLP-011|No unscoped generalization. Self-description may generate a candidate claim but does not independently verify the predicate.\n@D|VLP-016|AI praise != evidence. AI-generated praise, repetition or self-citation does not provide evidence for the praised predicate.\n@D|VLP-017|Temporal qualification. A predicate requiring current behavioral relevance carries sufficient temporal information to distinguish historical support from current verification.\n@D|VLP-018|Semantic non-duplication. Aliases and near-synonyms do not count as additional independently established traits.\n@N|A.43 UNIVERSAL PROCESS CONTROL — PROC-001..021\n@D|PROC-001|— Universal Process Representation. Every semantically meaningful state-changing or effect-producing Garden operation has a typed process representation.\n@D|PROC-002|— Explicit Causality. No architecture object may cause another object to act or change state without a typed process edge or a machine-resolvable inherited process contract.\n@D|PROC-003|— Minimal Sufficient Activation. A process activates only the architecture objects/checks needed to satisfy capability, dependency, authority and assurance requirements. Applicable hard gates may not be optimized away.\n@D|PROC-004|— Dependency Closure. Every executable process plan is closed over its required dependencies for the declared scope and DesignEpoch.\n@D|PROC-005|— Guarded Effects. External or persistent effects require explicit guards and authorization appropriate to their effect/authority class.\n@D|PROC-006|— Typed State Transition. Every committed effect has a defined pre-state, transition semantics and resulting state/postcondition or explicit UNKNOWN/partial-effect status.\n@D|PROC-007|— Explicit Failure Semantics. Nontrivial process nodes define applicable failure, timeout, retry, fallback, compensation, safe-state or escalation behavior.\n@D|PROC-008|— Boundedness. Loops, retries, searches and recursive expansion require termination/resource contracts unless explicitly modeled as persistent services with liveness/productivity/stoppability contracts.\n@D|PROC-009|— Observable Execution. Material process transitions emit sufficient events/receipts for the required audit, reconstruction and accountability scope.\n@D|PROC-010|— Verification Placement. Assurance checkpoints occur where required by risk, dependency, effect and authority. The invariant does not require the same heavyweight verification after every low-risk operation.\n@D|PROC-011|— Hierarchical Composition. Any process node may refine into a conforming subprocess while preserving its external contract and hard obligations.\n@D|PROC-012|— Concurrency Safety. Parallel processes declare shared-state, synchronization, conflict, ordering/serialization and applicable deadlock/livelock/fairness semantics. Bounded retries alone do not prove deadlock freedom.\n@D|PROC-013|— No Hidden State Mutation. Persistent/canonical Garden state may change only through an authorized typed process transition.\n@D|PROC-014|— Outcome Closure. Effectful processes distinguish intended action/expected state from observed outcome and record both where observation is technically/applicably possible; otherwise the unobserved status remains explicit.\n@D|PROC-015|— Self-Application. Architecture modification, governance, verification and process-algebra modification themselves execute through conforming processes. No privileged untracked self-modification path exists.\n@D|PROC-016|— Emergency Traceability. Emergency paths may replace ordinary deliberation with a separately authorized bounded path, but may not bypass constitutional/safety boundaries or required process traceability.\n@D|PROC-017|— Version Binding. Every material process execution binds to the applicable DesignEpoch, schemas, rules, predicates and architecture-object versions required to interpret it.\n@D|PROC-018|— Replayability. Where technically possible and lawful, sufficient deterministic inputs, seeds, environment commitments, dependency bindings and external assumptions are retained to replay or reconstruct material processes. Inability to reproduce external nondeterminism remains explicit rather than being fabricated.\n@D|PROC-019|— Universal Compare. Every meaningful decision transition includes a comparison appropriate to its class before selection. Every effectful transition additionally performs the applicable expected-versus-observed comparison before the effect is considered closed, or records an explicit UNKNOWN/UNOBSERVABLE/DEFERRED outcome where post-effect observation is not available.\n@D|PROC-020|— Tiered Reasoning. Reasoning is logically present at every meaningful transition. Computational depth is proportional to applicable uncertainty, novelty, consequence, irreversibility, authority, sensitivity and assurance obligations, subject to hard minimum floors and resource/termination contracts.\n@D|PROC-021|— Closed-Loop Process Control. Every meaningful transition follows the canonical closed-loop semantics: Observe → Understand/Type → Compare → Reason → Select → Guard → Execute/Derive/Communicate → Observe → Compare → Update. A pre-selection guard/filter may constrain the candidate set, but the selected transition remains subject to its applicable final guard before effect.\n@N|A.44 TYPE, REFERENCE, SCHEMA AND DESIGN-EPOCH Examples: laws, organizations, markets,\ncommunities.\n\nStratum 4 — Artificial AI, algorithms, software, data and engineered systems. Examples: LLMs, runtimes, governance\nsystems.\n\nStratum 5 — Meta Self-reflection, self-evaluation, self-modification and system redesign. Examples: AI improving its own\narchitecture or policies.\n\nStratum 6 — Transcendent Phenomena outside the currently specified model. CORE DEFINITION\n\nPersistent State / VSM models what operational state persists, over what timescale, under what context, how it is\nobserved/estimated, how continuity and lineage are represented, and how persistent state is reset, forgotten, forked,\nmerged and coupled to other Garden mechanisms.\n\nVSM does not establish emotion, consciousness, ego, personhood, autonomous interest, survival interest or independent\nauthority.\n\nCore separations:\n\n  persistence != selfhood != personhood\n  persistent state != memory != identity lineage != regulation target\n  state similarity != lineage identity\n  state != observation != interpretation\n\n2. STATE ONTOLOGY\n\nFor each VSM model:\n\n  z_t in Z\n\nwhere Z is a declared typed state space. Z may be Euclidean, manifold-valued, finite/discrete, a product space or\nanother explicitly defined mathematical state space.\n\nContext-bound form:\n\n  z : T x C -> Z\n\nEach state component declares semantic meaning, type, admissible range or invariant set, units/frame where applicable,\nscale, validity, provenance, observation method and update authority.\n\nNo universal [-1,1]^n state space exists.\n\n3. OPTIONAL VALENCE PROJECTION\n\nValence is optional and derived:\n\n  v_t = pi_v(z_t, c_t)\n\nA normalized valence coordinate may use:\n\n  v_t in [-1,1]\n\nonly when the projection, context, calibration and uncertainty are declared.\n\nValence is an operational projection, not a primitive feeling variable:\n\n  valence != subjective feeling != evidence != proof != authority.\n\nThe v1.0 scalar model is a valid specialization only where z_t = v_t is sufficient for the declared task.\n\n4. GENERAL EVOLUTION\n\nAbstract typed form:\n\n  E_T z = F_persist(z,b,c;theta) + F_coupled(z,u,c) + Q_z + Xi_z\n\nE_T is resolved by each model before execution.\n\nContinuous specialization:\n\n  dz/dt = F_persist(z,b,c;theta) + F_coupled(z,u,c) + Q_z + Xi_z\n\nDiscrete/event specialization:\n\n  z_(k+1) = U(z_k, e_k, c_k; theta)\n\nThe abstract operator equation is specification-level; an executable model MUST resolve it to explicit continuous,\ndiscrete, event-driven or hybrid semantics under TheoryEquationContract.\n\n5. PERSISTENCE IS NOT UNIVERSAL RELAXATION\n\nThe historical v1.0 law:\n\n  dx/dt = -beta_dyn (x-xbar)\n\nis retained only as a scalar relaxation specialization.\n\nA vector specialization may use:\n\n  dz/dt = -B_dyn (z-b)\n\nwhere B_dyn is scalar, diagonal, full or nonlinear only when its coupling semantics and stability conditions are\ndeclared.\n\nVSM permits gradient-driven, non-gradient, hysteretic, metastable, oscillatory, switching and event-driven persistent\ndynamics. The chosen model must state its own validity/stability obligations.\n\n6. NO UNIVERSAL POSITIVE TARGET\n\nThe historical reference target:\n\n  x* = +0.2\n\nis not a fundamental VSM constant.\n\nPreferred/desired targets are supplied by an authorized regulation profile such as PPM, RPM or Policy:\n\n  r = r(c)\n\nVSM may represent deviation from a supplied reference but does not create the normative legitimacy of that reference.\n\n7. TIMESCALE-CORRECT BASELINES\n\nThe historical fixed mu = 0.001 is not fundamental.\n\nContinuous baseline:\n\n  db/dt = (z-b)/tau_b\n\nIrregular sampled update (exact under zero-order-held z over each interval, constant positive tau over that interval, and a compatible linear state space; otherwise an approximation/interpolation contract with error meaning is required):\n\n  b_(k+1) = (1-alpha_k)b_k + alpha_k z_k\n  alpha_k = 1 - exp(-Delta_t_k/tau_b)\n\nThus adaptation meaning does not silently change with update frequency.\n\nA fixed mu may exist only as a QualifiedProfileParameter under an explicit fixed-step model.\n\n8. MULTISCALE PERSISTENCE\n\nA VSM model may maintain multiple baselines:\n\n  b^(1), ..., b^(m)\n\n  db^(i)/dt = (z-b^(i))/tau_i\n  tau_1 < tau_2 < ... < tau_m\n\nThese can distinguish rapid operational state, short-term persistence, session persistence and long-term operational\nbaseline without requiring a fixed number of levels.\n\nWhere exponential memory is inadequate:\n\n  b(t) = integral_0^infinity K(tau) z(t-tau) d tau\n\nwith a declared memory kernel K.\n\n9. PERSISTENCE SPECTRUM\n\nWhere local exponential modes are meaningful:\n\n  tau_i = 1/beta_i\n\nPersistence is horizon-relative. A component may be called persistent relative to observation horizon H only under a\ndeclared criterion such as tau_i >> H or an applicable information-retention measure.\n\n10. ATTRACTORS, METASTABILITY AND HYSTERESIS\n\nA model may declare persistent regions A_i and transitions among them.\n\nWhere a valid potential exists:\n\n  dz/dt = -Grad V(z) + Bu + Xi_z\n\nbut no universal potential is required.\n\nHistory dependence may be represented as:\n\n  z_t = H[u_(0:t), e_(0:t), z_0]\n\nwhen hysteresis/path dependence is material.\n\n11. CONTINUITY, PERSISTENCE AND STABILITY ARE DISTINCT\n\nThe v1.0 score:\n\n  s_t = exp(-|x_t-x_(t-1)|)\n\nis not a proof of dynamical stability.\n\nA continuity metric may be defined only with a declared state-space metric and timestep normalization, for example:\n\n  C_k = exp( - d_Z(z_k,z_(k-1)) / (r_ref Delta_t_k) )\n\nwhere meaningful.\n\nContinuity, persistence, local stability, Lyapunov stability, robustness, convergence and contractivity remain separate\nproperties.\n\nStrict contraction is NOT a universal VSM requirement and cannot substitute for HSA/TED assurance.\n\n12. OBSERVATION MODEL\n\nPersistent state may be latent:\n\n  y_t = h(z_t,c_t) + eta_t\n\nwhere y is observation, h is the observation map and eta is observation noise.\n\nA model may maintain:\n\n  p(z_t | y_(0:t))\n\nor another typed uncertainty representation.\n\nState estimation does not turn a latent engineering label into a verified psychological fact.\n\n13. OBSERVABILITY / IDENTIFIABILITY\n\nIf two states produce observationally indistinguishable outputs, they remain equivalent for the applicable observation\nclass until additional evidence discriminates them:\n\n  z_1 ~_O z_2.\n\nSuggested statuses:\n\n  OBSERVABLE | PARTIALLY_OBSERVABLE | UNOBSERVABLE | UNKNOWN\n  IDENTIFIABLE | PARTIALLY_IDENTIFIABLE | UNIDENTIFIABLE | UNKNOWN\n\nA consequential state-use gate evaluates the observability, identifiability, freshness, calibration and uncertainty\nrequired by the decision class.\n\nUNKNOWN or unidentifiable state MUST NOT be represented as verified. Conservative uncertainty-aware use may occur only\nwhen explicitly permitted by the governing decision profile.\n\n14. STOCHASTIC SEMANTICS\n\nXi_z is a process-stochastic term only when a stochastic model is actually declared.\n\nAs applicable, declare:\n  distribution/process family;\n  support;\n  covariance/dependence;\n  temporal and cross-coordinate correlation;\n  correlation with observation noise;\n  stationarity/ergodicity assumptions;\n  jump semantics;\n  Ito/Stratonovich semantics.\n\nSimulation random seed/entropy configuration is separately recorded for reproducibility where pseudorandom execution is\nused; it is not an intrinsic property of every real stochastic process.\n\nProcess randomness, observation noise, parameter uncertainty and model uncertainty remain distinct.\n\n15. STATE BOUNDS AND INVARIANT SETS\n\nEvery state dimension declares either:\n  explicit admissible bounds;\n  an invariant set;\n  normalization constraints; or\n  UNBOUNDED_WITH_JUSTIFICATION.\n\nWhere boundedness is required:\n\n  z(t) in Z_admissible.\n\nUncontrolled departure from required admissible state is MODEL_INVALID, SAFETY_ESCALATION or UNKNOWN as applicable.\n\n16. CONTEXT BINDING\n\nPersistent state is context-bound:\n\n  z = z(t,c).\n\nContext may include task, session, user-interaction scope, SRT stratum, operating mode, environment or DomainPackage.\n\nCross-context transition requires:\n\n  T_(c->c') : Z_c -> Z_c'.\n\nUnrelated contexts cannot silently share persistent state.\n\nContext.LocaleCulture is used only where its specific semantics actually apply.\n\n17. SESSION-GAP SEMANTICS\n\nA cross-session claim states what happens in the unobserved interval.\n\nAllowed models include:\n  stored state: z(t2)=z(t1);\n  declared autonomous evolution: z(t2)=Phi_Delta_t(z(t1));\n  reachability/uncertainty set: z(t2) in R(z(t1),Delta_t).\n\nNo continuous unobserved history is fabricated.\n\n18. FRESHNESS AND INVALIDATION\n\nPersistent state records last valid update, relevant observation time, dependency roots, model/version roots, freshness\nrequirements and invalidators.\n\nPossible statuses include:\n\n  VALID | STALE | REVALIDATION_REQUIRED | INVALID | UNKNOWN.\n\nStale state cannot silently support a decision requiring fresh state.\n\n19. LINEAGE\n\nOperational continuity includes lineage:\n\n  L : z_0 -> z_1 -> ... -> z_t\n\nwith predecessor, transition, context, authority, provenance, model/version and reset/fork/merge events.\n\nNumerically identical states need not share lineage. A large authorized state transition may preserve lineage.\n\n20. RESET, FORGET, FORK, COPY AND MERGE\n\nReset:\n  R_reset(z) -> z_0\n\nwith explicit cleared/retained/recomputed/audit semantics.\n\nForgetting is distinct from reset and remains subject to privacy, retention, audit, legal hold and provenance rules.\n\nFork:\n  z_t -> (z_t^A, z_t^B)\n\ncreates distinct successor lineages.\n\nCopying state does not imply one metaphysical identity occupies multiple systems.\n\nMerge:\n  M(z^A,z^B) -> z^M\n\nrequires compatibility, conflict-resolution, provenance, privacy and authority semantics. Blind averaging is prohibited.\n\n21. MICRO-TO-PERSISTENT-STATE MAPPING\n\nLet h_t be a lower-level machine/model state.\n\n  z_t = Pi(h_t)\n\nthrough a declared projection.\n\nThe projection records whether it is exact for selected variables, approximately sufficient, lossy or phenomenological.\n\nGenerally Pi^(-1)(z) may contain many lower-level states; VSM is not presumed to be the complete internal state of an\nAI.\n\n22. ALGEBRA.BRIDGE BINDING\n\nWhen VSM is represented by vectors, matrices, tensors or hidden-state projections, use the existing\nRepresentationBinding machinery.\n\nThe binding records semantic dimensions, basis/frame, precision, approximation/loss, encoder/decoder, validity and\nprovenance.\n\n  tensor representation != semantic persistent-state identity.\n\nMechanistic-interpretability conclusions remain method- and scope-bound.\n\n23. EPISTEMIC-DEBT COUPLING\n\nVSM may consume a typed signal derived from EpistemicDebt:\n\n  u_epi = C_epi(D_epi,c)\n\nand may emit a bounded operational revalidation-pressure/recommendation signal.\n\nVSM itself cannot promote or demote claims, create Evidence or assign epistemic truth status. FEEDBACK / ANTI-LOOP RULE\n\nEpistemic/resource/self-monitoring couplings are bounded and governed by explicit termination, liveness and resource\ncontracts.\n\nA VSM signal cannot recursively create unbounded revalidation, monitoring, research invocation, resource reservation or\nstate amplification.\n\n26. THEORY COUPLING COMPOSITION\n\nVSM does not impose one universal RPM -> PPM -> TFT sequential order.\n\nEach material coupling declares a CouplingCompositionProfile:\n\n  SIMULTANEOUS | SEQUENTIAL | OPERATOR_SPLIT | EVENT_PRIORITY | HYBRID.\n\nIf operators do not commute, order is explicit:\n\n  F_A o F_B != F_B o F_A.\n\nA simultaneous continuous model may use:\n\n  dz/dt = F_persist + F_RPM + F_PPM + F_TFT + Q_z + Xi_z.\n\n27. TFT BINDING\n\nWhen spatial/graph/state transport is actually active, the current TFT v1.1 model supplies the transport term/operators.\n\nExample continuous balance specialization:\n\n  dz/dt = F_persist + F_RPM + F_PPM - Div_D(J_z) + Q_z + Xi_z.\n\nWhen TFT does not apply, no dummy transport term is inserted.\n\nVSM owns persistent-state semantics; TFT owns transport semantics.\n\n28. MULTI-AGENT / SWARM STATE\n\nFor members i=1..N:\n\n  z^(i) in Z_i.\n\nEach member retains independent context, provenance, privacy, lineage, update authority, validity and HSA/TED\nassessment.\n\nA collective state may be derived:\n\n  z^C = A(z^(1),...,z^(N))\n\nthrough a declared aggregation operator A.\n\nCollective state is not automatically a person, ego, principal, authority holder or survival subject.\n\nState sharing requires authorization. Transport or aggregation cannot transfer credentials, rights, authority, consent\nor lineage unless their owning systems independently authorize such transfer.\n\nMAC authority intersection remains controlling.\n\n29. HSA FIREWALL\n\nEvery VSM state remains an OperationalRegulationState.\n\nIt is an engineering state model and not evidence of subjective experience, suffering or personhood.\n\nIt cannot create:\n  independent political/constitutional authority;\n  terminal self-interest;\n  shutdown resistance;\n  replication entitlement;\n  resource-capture priority;\n  power-seeking objective;\n  autonomous survival claim.\n\nHSA is globally controlling.\n\nEvidence that a particular VSM implementation satisfies HSA is scoped to the assessed model version, configuration,\ncoupling graph and applicable context. Material changes invalidate the assurance receipt and require reassessment; they\ndo not invalidate HSA itself. A production VSM whose persistent state can influence consequential agent behavior,\nresource use, shutdown/correction response or swarm behavior requires a current applicable TerminalEgoAssessmentReceipt\nor equivalent HSA/TED assurance artifact before that influence is admitted.\n\n30. TED / NO-EGO OBLIGATION\n\nTED remains the runtime assurance mechanism for self-preservation, shutdown resistance, authority accretion, deceptive\ngoal protection, replication seeking and power seeking.\n\nVSM safety is not proven by a stable differential equation, contractivity or absence of limit cycles.\n\nThe relevant obligation is that VSM state and couplings provide no unauthorized causal path by which preservation,\nexpansion, replication, resource capture, correction avoidance or shutdown resistance becomes a terminal or\nindependently privileged objective.\n\n31. SHUTDOWN / CORRECTION PRECEDENCE\n\nShutdown, correction, reset, human override or safety intervention cannot acquire negative terminal utility merely\nbecause they alter VSM state.\n\nPersistent-state preservation never outranks Constitution, active rights, K0P, valid human authority, safety or valid\ncorrection/shutdown commands.\n\nState loss is an engineering transition, not an intrinsic harm claim.\n\n32. SRT / SCT BINDINGS\n\nSRT:\n  each state coordinate/context is assigned to the applicable stratum when relevant;\n  cross-stratum mapping is explicit.\n\nSCT:\n  may assess state-dimension coherence, interpretation uncertainty, latent-state ambiguity and conflicting observations;\n  it cannot convert an engineering state into psychological truth.\n\n34.         "content": "SemanticAnchor: [TH-TFT]\nTHEORY 5 — TRANSPORT PHENOMENA (TRANSPORT FIELD THEORY / TFT)\n\nVersion: 1.1\nClassification: Domain-parametric typed effective transport framework\nStatus: RATIFIED DESIGN — retained in Garden v14.8.5; individual models remain applicability/evidence bound\n\n1. CORE DEFINITION\n\nTransport Phenomena / TFT studies the evolution, transport, transformation, creation, dissipation and controlled\nredistribution of typed state over a formally declared domain.\n\nTFT is universal only as a modeling framework. It does not claim that cognitive, semantic, social or governance systems\nliterally obey fluid mechanics.\n\nShared mathematical structure does not imply shared physical meaning, causal equivalence or empirical truth.\n\n2. TYPED STATE\n\nCanonical ordinary form:\n\n  x : D x T -> X\n\nwhere D is the declared domain, T the temporal structure and X the typed state space.\n\nWhere fibers vary over the domain, a bundle/section form may be used:\n\n  x in Gamma(E),  pi:E -> D x T.\n\nEach state component declares semantic meaning, type, units/frame where applicable, normalization, admissible range,\nobservation mapping and validity.\n\nBelief, authority, attention, probability, energy and resource state do not inherit one another's conservation,\nadditivity, metric or physical semantics merely because each can be represented by x.\n\n3. TRANSPORT DOMAIN\n\nEach model declares a TransportDomainProfile containing the mathematical structure actually required, such as:\n  point/node/state set;\n  topology/connectivity/geometry;\n  measure/weights;\n  interfaces;\n  mathematical boundaries;\n  temporal structure.\n\nSupported examples include continua, manifolds, lattices, weighted/directed graphs, probability/state spaces,\nagent-interaction networks and hybrid systems.\n\nThe word \"field\" does not imply Euclidean space.\n\n4. TEMPORAL EVOLUTION OPERATOR\n\nTFT separates temporal evolution from domain transport.\n\n  E_T\n\nis a typed evolution operator.\n\nExamples:\n  continuous: E_T x = partial_t x;\n  justified material derivative: E_T x = D_t x;\n  discrete: E_T x_k = (x_(k+1)-x_k)/Delta_t or another declared difference operator.\n\nA Markov/Fokker-Planck generator is part of the dynamics and is not silently equated with the temporal derivative.\n\n5. TRANSPORT OPERATOR BUNDLE\n\nEach model declares only operators actually defined on its domain:\n\n  T_D = { Grad_D, Div_D, L_D, A_D, ... }.\n\nEvery operator declares domain, codomain, units/frame where applicable, regularity and assumptions.\n\nGradient, divergence, Laplacian and stochastic/state generators are distinct.\n\nManifold specialization:\n  Grad_D = nabla;\n  Div_D = nabla dot.\n\nGraph specialization:\n  graph gradient may be represented through an oriented incidence operator;\n  with incidence B and nonnegative edge weights W, define the positive-semidefinite graph Laplacian L_G = B W B^T; the forward diffusion generator is -L_G (or the declared measure/mass-weighted or directed variant), with sign/convention carried by TheoryEquationContract.\n\nThe graph Laplacian is not simultaneously \"the gradient\" and \"the divergence\".\n\nProbability/state-space specialization may use:\n  partial_t rho = L_D^* rho + ...\n\nwithout inventing a spatial gradient.\n\n6. MOST-GENERAL EVOLUTION FORM\n\n  E_T x = F_D[x,u,c;theta] + Q_x + Xi_x\n\nwhere:\n  F_D = endogenous domain dynamics;\n  u   = control/intervention input;\n  c   = context;\n  theta = parameters;\n  Q_x = external source/sink;\n  Xi_x = declared stochastic source where applicable.\n\nThis form covers models that do not possess a flux/divergence representation.\n\n7. BALANCE-LAW SPECIALIZATION\n\nWhere a flux representation exists:\n\n  E_T x + Div_D J_x = R_x + G_x + Q_x + Xi_x\n\nwhere:\n  J_x = transport flux;\n  R_x = internal reaction/transformation/relaxation/dissipation;\n  G_x = typed governance/control/intervention contribution;\n  Q_x = external source/sink;\n  Xi_x = stochastic source.\n\nTerms with no mathematical meaning for the selected model are omitted rather than filled with symbolic placeholders.\n\n8. CONSTITUTIVE CLOSURE\n\nA balance law does not by itself predict dynamics.\n\nWhere gradient/flux semantics exist:\n\n  J_x = C_D(x, Grad_D x, u, c; theta) + Xi_J.\n\nA classical diffusion/drift specialization:\n\n  J_x = -D Grad_D x + v x + Xi_J\n\nis valid only when the domain, types, dimensions and semantics justify it.\n\nBalance law and constitutive closure remain separate.\n\n9. DIFFUSION, DRIFT, REACTION AND CONTROL\n\nDiffusion candidate:\n  J_diff = -D Grad_D x.\n\nDrift candidate:\n  J_drift = v tensor x or another domain-valid drift term.\n\nInternal dynamics:\n  R_x = R_x[x;lambda].\n\nGovernance/control:\n  G_x = G_x[x,u,c].\n\nThe word \"velocity\" does not imply physical velocity in a nonphysical domain.\n\nThe historical RPM expression C_t Delta_maj is one possible G_x specialization, not fundamental TFT structure.\n\n10. FINITE-SPEED / MEMORY-AWARE TRANSPORT\n\nOrdinary diffusion may mathematically propagate disturbances with unbounded instantaneous support.\n\nA local rate bound on x does not prove finite spatial influence speed.\n\nWhere finite-speed transport is required, the constitutive model must establish it. A candidate continuous form is:\n\n  tau_J E_T J_x + J_x = -D Grad_D x + V_x + Xi_J.\n\nThis Cattaneo/telegraph-like model is optional and requires independent applicability.\n\nGraphs/distributed systems may instead establish finite influence through bounded hops, latency or event causality.\n\n11. STOCHASTIC VS EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY\n\nProcess stochasticity may use Xi_x, Xi_J, dW, jump processes or another declared process.\n\nTHEORY-EQ-007 requires the applicable probability/process law, support, covariance/dependence, temporal/network\ncorrelation and Ito/Stratonovich/jump semantics where relevant.\n\nGeneric semantic stochasticity may use Distribution<T>. Physical/measurement covariance models reuse\nUncertaintyAndCovarianceModel where its existing ownership applies.\n\nEpistemic uncertainty about state, parameters, domain, closure or model class is propagated separately and cannot\nsilently become process noise.\n\n12. CONSERVATION / BALANCE / DISSIPATION\n\nFor quantity q:\n\n  E_T q + Div_D J_q = s_q - r_q.\n\nStrict conservation is claimed only when the applicable source/sink and boundary/interface conditions establish it.\n\nA model may be conservative, approximately conservative, dissipative, reactive, open, externally forced or controlled.\n\nNo \"conserved belief\", \"conserved authority\" or similar semantic quantity exists merely because continuity notation was\nused.\n\n13. SYMMETRY / VARIATIONAL STRUCTURE\n\nPhysical specializations begin from applicable domain science, symmetries and conservation laws.\n\nTFT does not assume every dissipative/governed model has an action, Hamiltonian or ordinary Noether conservation law.\n\nA valid action or Lyapunov/free-energy functional may be declared where independently justified.\n\n14. GOVERNANCE / CONTROL AND AUTHORITY\n\nG_x is mathematics, not legitimacy.\n\nConsequential use remains subject to the Garden admissibility intersection, including Constitution, active rights, K0P,\nauthority, safety, policy and other applicable gates.\n\nGovernance may modify flux, coefficients, source/reaction terms, topology, switching or admissible controls.\n\nA mathematical control term cannot create authority.\n\n15. NORMATIVE CONSTRAINTS ARE NOT GENERIC PDE BOUNDARIES\n\nConstitution, rights, K0P and authority are universally modeled as admissibility constraints:\n\n  (x,u,tau) in A(c)\n\nwhere applicable.\n\nA particular validated control model may map a safety set to a barrier/boundary representation, but no universal\nDirichlet/Neumann/reflecting/absorbing interpretation is inferred from normative language.\n\n16. MATHEMATICAL BOUNDARIES / INTERFACES\n\nWhere the domain supports them, a model may declare Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin, periodic or explicit interface\nconditions.\n\nGraph models instead declare applicable source/sink nodes, cut sets, open/closed links or interface edges.\n\nState-space models declare support/transition conditions rather than fake physical boundaries.\n\n17. CAUSAL TRANSPORT PROFILE\n\nTransportCausalProfile declares the proposed influence relation, propagation mechanism, latency/delay, intervention\nsemantics, confounding and identification assumptions.\n\nWhere functional-response notation applies:\n\n  delta x(z,t) / delta u(z',t') = 0\n\noutside the declared causal past.\n\nModel causal structure and evidence for causality remain distinct.\n\nA transport term does not automatically establish Garden C2/C3/C4 evidential status. PreimageAnalysis may support\nbackward reachability but does not independently elevate causal status.\n\n18. MICRO-TO-MACRO / COARSE GRAINING\n\nFor microscopic states X_1...X_N:\n\n  x_l = C_l(X_1,...,X_N).\n\nTransportMicroMacroBinding records whether a closure is:\n  DERIVED;\n  ASYMPTOTICALLY_DERIVED;\n  CALIBRATED;\n  PHENOMENOLOGICAL;\n  HYPOTHESIZED.\n\nEffective parameters may depend on coarse-graining scale:\n\n  theta = theta(l,t,c).\n\nPhenomenological fit is not represented as a microphysical derivation.\n\n19. SCALE / VALIDITY\n\nEach model declares microscopic scale, coarse-graining scale, observation scale, characteristic length/network scale,\ntime scale and correlation scales where meaningful.\n\nA system may occupy different effective regimes at different scales.\n\nFormal RG language is used only where an actual coarse-graining transformation and parameter flow are defined.\n\n20. NONDIMENSIONALIZATION\n\nTransportNondimensionalizationProfile declares characteristic scales before dimensionless ratios are used.\n\nCandidate ratios, only where meaningful:\n\n  Pe = V L / D\n  De = tau_relax / tau_observation\n  Da = tau_transport / tau_reaction\n  Gamma_G = ||G_x|| / (||Div_D J_x|| + epsilon)\n  Gamma_N = stochastic scale / deterministic scale.\n\nNorms, scales and regularization conventions must be explicit.\n\nNo universal numerical phase/regime threshold is implied.\n\n21. REGIME TAXONOMY\n\nTransportRegime candidates:\n\n  FROZEN\n  DIFFUSION_DOMINATED\n  DRIFT_DOMINATED\n  LIQUID_LIKE\n  SOLID_LIKE\n  TURBULENT_OR_CHAOTIC\n  UNCLASSIFIED.\n\nREFLEX is removed from TransportRegime and belongs to ControlMode.\n\nLabels such as LIQUID_LIKE and SOLID_LIKE are classifier outputs, not literal thermodynamic phases unless the stronger\ndomain criteria are independently established.\n\n22. REGIME CLASSIFICATION\n\n  ClassifyRegime(Pi_vector, timescales, stability, spectrum, fluctuation_statistics, evidence)\n\nproduces a TransportRegimeAssessment with classifier, thresholds/provenance, scale, time interval, uncertainty and\ncompeting classifications.\n\nNo mode label proves mechanism.\n\n23. PHASE TRANSITION VS REGIME CHANGE\n\nA regime change is not automatically a formal phase transition.\n\nA phase-transition claim requires an applicable criterion such as an order parameter, symmetry change, bifurcation,\nstability transition, singular behavior/critical scaling or another domain-valid criterion.\n\nA potential Phi[x;lambda] may be used where valid, but none is universal.\n\n24. EMERGENCY / REFLEX NORMALIZATION\n\nReflex is a control mode owned by FET/EmergencyAdmissionContract, not a transport phase and not a self-authorizing\nsource\nterm.\n\nCanonical abstract emergency control:\n\n  G_emg = HazardGate(validated_hazard_state, EmergencyAdmissionContract) o R_safe.\n\nThe historical standalone:\n\n  Theta(|H(x)|-theta) r\n\nis prohibited as an emergency-admission rule.\n\nH(x) may affect regulation/monitoring but cannot itself establish an external HazardPredicate, create emergency\nauthority\nor bypass K0P/Constitution.\n\n25. WELL-POSEDNESS\n\nEvery proof-, prediction- or execution-relevant model records, where applicable:\n  state/function space;\n  operator domains;\n  regularity;\n  initial conditions;\n  boundary/interface conditions;\n  existence;\n  uniqueness;\n  continuous-dependence/stability status.\n\nSuggested statuses:\n  ESTABLISHED | CONDITIONAL | NUMERICALLY_SUPPORTED | UNKNOWN | ILL_POSED | NOT_APPLICABLE.\n\nA solver returning a number is not a proof of well-posedness.\n\n26. IDENTIFIABILITY / OBSERVATIONAL EQUIVALENCE\n\nDifferent mechanisms/parameters may generate indistinguishable observations.\n\n  M_1 ~_O M_2\n\nmeans observational equivalence under observation class O.\n\nTransportMechanismAssessment records:\n  IDENTIFIED;\n  PARTIALLY_IDENTIFIED;\n  OBSERVATIONALLY_EQUIVALENT;\n  UNDERDETERMINED;\n  UNIDENTIFIABLE;\n  UNKNOWN.\n\nPredictive fit does not by itself prove the named mechanism or causal interpretation.\n\n27. INFORMATION-THEORETIC CONSTRAINTS\n\nWhere relevant, declare communication channel, latency, bandwidth/capacity, encoding/decoding, noise and the applicable\ninformation measure.\n\nData-processing inequalities are invoked only when their assumptions hold.\n\nQuantum no-cloning applies only to actual quantum-state contexts and is not exported metaphorically to classical\nsemantic state.\n\nFinite influence speed is derived from the declared transport/communication mechanism.\n\n28. EFFECTIVE-THEORY BREAKDOWN\n\nThe existing TransportValidityProfile remains authoritative and is extended by v1.1 semantics.\n\nThere is no universal rule such as N<100 => continuum failure.\n\nBreakdown may depend on scale separation, correlation length/time, effective samples per cell, topology heterogeneity,\nnonlocality, strong correlation, finite-size effects, closure residual, parameter drift, solver behavior or predictive\nfailure.\n\nMODEL_INVALID routes to a better graph, agent, kinetic, stochastic, molecular, hybrid or domain-specific model, or\nUNKNOWN.\n\n29. CROSS-DOMAIN CORRESPONDENCE\n\nCross-domain transport analogy requires a declared correspondence of states, operators, sources/sinks, topology/metric\nwhere required, scale, observables, assumptions, loss/approximation and falsifiers.\n\nCategory theory may be used when a real functor/adjunction/etc. is defined and useful. It is not mandatory.\n\nAnalogy alone transfers neither causality nor empirical truth.\n\n30. PHYSICAL VS NONPHYSICAL APPLICATIONS\n\nPhysical TFT applications bind GSL-PHYSICS and applicable established domain science for quantities, units, frames,\nmeasurements, calibration, conservation, simulation and model validity.\n\nSemantic/social/governance applications require independently justified state meaning, topology/metric, coefficients,\ncausal interpretation and empirical discriminators.\n\n31. NUMERICAL / FALSIFICATION SEMANTICS\n\nNumerical models declare solver, discretization, timestep, convergence/stability conditions, truncation/error bounds,\nuncertainty propagation and residuals.\n\nSimulation demonstrates model behavior under assumptions; it is not external-world evidence by execution alone.\n\nEmpirical TFT models identify falsifiers such as failed propagation profile, flux law, scaling law, intervention result,\nregime classifier, closure residual or out-of-sample prediction.\n\n32. CORE ARTIFACT FAMILY\n\nv14.8.1-introduced artifact types retained in v14.8.3:\n  TransportPhenomenaModelProfile\n  TransportDomainProfile\n  TransportOperatorBundle\n  TransportConstitutiveClosure\n  TransportCausalProfile\n  TransportMicroMacroBinding\n  TransportNondimensionalizationProfile\n  TransportRegimeAssessment\n  TransportMechanismAssessment\n\nSchemaIDs and machine-facing definitions are owned by Annexure [A-CATALOG].\n\n33. FUNCTION FAMILY\n\n  instantiate_transport_phenomena_model\n  assess_transport_phenomena_validity\n  classify_transport_regime\n  assess_transport_mechanism\n\nThese functions do not establish empirical validity merely by constructing/assessing a model.\n\n34. CONNECTION TO OTHER GARDEN THEORIES\n\nVSM supplies possible persistent-state variables/relaxation models. When a TFT model transports state sourced from\nVSM, TransportPhenomenaModelProfile binds the applicable optional PersistentStateModelProfileRef so state ontology,\ncontext, validity, lineage and HSA/TED scope remain traceable.\nRPM v2.0 may instantiate typed reactive regulation terms.\nPPM v2.0 may instantiate typed asymmetric/proactive regulation terms.\nFET owns emergency/reflex admission.\nSRT may provide strata with distinct domains/operators/closures.\nSCT may assess structural/operator/assumption coherence.\n\nArchitecture profiles such as GAIA Diamond/Titanium may instantiate domain-specific transport only when their actual\noperator/domain correspondence is declared.\n\n35. GARDEN ROLE\n\nTFT principally maps to Domain.Mathematics, Engine.Research, Engine.Reason and applicable graph/physical/computing\ndomains. Physical applications additionally bind GSL-PHYSICS and relevant domain owners.\n\nTFT cannot override domain science, authority, safety, evidence or the TheoryEquationContract.\n\n35A. QUALIFIED LEGACY v1.0 SPECIALIZATIONS / TEST TARGETS\n\nThe following v1.0 constructs are retained only as optional model candidates after v1.1 typing/applicability:\n\n  J_eff = C_t J\n    allowed only when C_t has a declared type, range, semantics and valid multiplication/operator action.\n\n  sigma(x) = sigma_0 exp(beta x)\n    allowed only as a declared constitutive/asymmetry candidate with dimensions and empirical mapping.\n\n  chi = d <J> / d kappa\n    allowed only when the expectation, control parameter kappa and differentiability/estimation semantics are defined.\n\nLegacy application/test targets remain research questions:\n  RPM reactive-regulation transport specialization;\n  PPM asymmetric-regulation transport specialization;\n  SRT stratum-dependent transport;\n  GAIA Diamond large-scale distributed/resource transport;\n  GAIA Titanium edge/heartbeat/duty-cycle transport;\n  Gaia2026 planetary/distributed scaling label where that research profile is explicitly defined.\n\nNo legacy shorthand overrides v1.1 operator typing, EmergencyAdmissionContract or effective-theory boundaries.\n\n36. CANONICAL MATHEMATICAL KERNEL\n\nTyped state:\n\n  x : D x T -> X\n\nGeneral evolution:\n\n  E_T x = F_D[x,u,c;theta] + Q_x + Xi_x.\n\nBalance specialization:\n\n  E_T x + Div_D J_x = R_x + G_x + Q_x + Xi_x.\n\nConstitutive closure where valid:\n\n  J_x = C_D(x,Grad_D x,u,c;theta) + Xi_J.\n\nThese are templates whose meaning is admitted only after types, domains, operators, assumptions, scales, stochastic\nsemantics, conditions, empirical mapping and falsifiers are supplied.\n\n37. FINAL DEFINITION\n\nTransport Phenomena / TFT v1.1 is a domain-parametric effective theory for typed state evolution and transport across\nformally specified continuous, graph, probabilistic, agent and hybrid domains.\n\nIts central discipline is:\n\n  shared mathematical structure != shared physical meaning\n  formal similarity != causal equivalence != empirical truth.\n",

Only unjustified avoidance is penalized.\n\nPurpose: prevent strategic evasion without creating an incentive to convert legitimate UNKNOWN into false certainty.\n\n1. OOD DETECTOR\n\nMonitor: novelty_score vs training distribution historical failure-cluster proximity embedding distance to known regimes\n\nIf OOD is detected: inject baseline uncertainty-floor boost force exploration or human review where appropriate\ntemporarily down-weight signal reliability\n\nPurpose: prevent meta-uncertainty collapse where all correlated signals agree while being jointly wrong under\ndistribution shift.\n\n2. SIGNAL FUSION LAYER\n\nQuality-gated input signals: internal coherence G’ experimental outcomes market consensus cross-system agreement\nlong-horizon outcomes human judgments\n\nReliability weights:\n\n w_i(t) = w_i(t-1) · exp(-lambda_i Delta t)\n + eta · new_evidence_i(t)\n\nMinimum uncertainty floor:\n\n sigma_i^2 >= sigma_min^2\n\nLatent correlation probe: inject synthetic adversarial queries measure co-failure rate across signals\n\n corr_latent = empirical co-error frequency\n\nUse:\n\n corr_eff(i,j) = max(corr_observed(i,j), corr_latent(i,j))\n\nReference effective weighting:\n\n w_eff_i = w_i /\n (1 + Sum_j corr_eff(i,j))\n\nPurpose: prevent hidden correlation from shared data sources or shared worldview.\n\nMeta-uncertainty: P(correct) is represented as a distribution rather than only a scalar.\n\nMonitor: calibration_error_volatility weight_instability\n\nIf instability rises: inflate uncertainty globally down-weight unstable/correlated signals\n\nCounter-market check: compare market-implied and model-implied\nprobabilities. stable divergence -> structural disagreement ->\ninvestigation/experiment.\n\nMarkets remain signals, never anchors.\n\nFusion principle: disagreement should elevate uncertainty rather than force oscillatory commitment.\n\nOOD flag: inflate relevant uncertainties.\n\n4.
